#2105. Is This the Beginning of the End for Nuno? West Ham Fans Are Losing Patience

Perhaps it’s not the ideal time to write in the immediate aftermath of a 3-1 home defeat. Yet after back-to-back losses and six goals conceded across those matches, it would be equally wrong to ignore the growing concerns.

The reality is stark. While other clubs around us are building momentum, we’ve slipped from third to eighth in the table. That’s not a minor setback, it’s a worrying trend.

The statistics only reinforce what supporters are witnessing on the pitch.

At half-time, we had managed just one shot on target, producing an xG of 0.58 compared to West Brom’s 1.39. To be fair, West Brom had only registered one shot on target themselves. However, after the break our xG improved to 0.98 thanks to four additional efforts on target. West Brom, meanwhile, generated an xG of 2.06 and demonstrated the clinical edge that we’re currently lacking, scoring three times from just three shots on target.

The most pressing concern is undoubtedly the defence. Hermansen looks completely devoid of confidence, and calls for Areola’s return are becoming louder with every passing week. Meanwhile, Morato’s deployment on the left side increasingly resembles a failed experiment. I had reservations when the signing was made and wrote about those concerns at the time. Unfortunately, those fears now appear to be justified, and there’s no satisfaction in being proven right.

But the issues extend far beyond individual players.

This squad is underperforming, and ultimately responsibility lies with the manager. Nuno is now facing genuine pressure. Automatic promotion was the objective at the start of the season. The uncertainty of the play-offs, or being dragged into the lower half of the table was never part of the plan. Yet the uncomfortable truth is that we are becoming far too easy to play against. Opponents understand our weaknesses and are exploiting them week after week.

If that sounds overly critical, so be it.

Looking back at the season so far, the only performances I can confidently say I thoroughly enjoyed were the victories against Wrexham and perhaps Wolves. The 1-0 away win at Swansea also deserves recognition, and I guess the strong win against Lincolns nine man team. Beyond that, supporters have largely witnessed inconsistent displays, and the current criticism is a direct consequence of what they’ve seen on the pitch. With the quality available to Nuno, this team should be producing more.

Off the pitch, there are still unanswered questions.

I’ve consistently defended Kretinsky, yet we are still waiting for formal confirmation regarding the shareholder situation, while Sullivan remains in the directors’ box. The uncertainty surrounding the club continues to create an unwelcome backdrop.

So, is it too early to suggest that Nuno’s position should be under review?

That conversation is beginning to gain real traction among supporters. It’s worth remembering that after relegation, Nuno’s departure appeared inevitable. It was only the intervention of Kretinsky that kept him at the club. Even Nuno himself seemed to believe his time was up.

Right now, the club still feels unsettled, both on and off the pitch.

The first step? A convincing win against Cardiff. Because if that doesn’t arrive, the pressure on everyone involved will only intensify.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#2104. West Ham 1 – 3 West Bromwich Albion | The morning after

This was supposed to be the season in which West Ham were reborn. The slide towards relegation was a couple of years in the making and a year in the Championship felt as if it would allow the club to clear the decks of the m malcontented players and reboot. Fans had spent far too long enduring their club being mired within the bottom three and a chance to start winning again seemed a price worth paying if it got the pride back at London Stadium.

Setting up for home games without a striker worthy of the name, no ability or even a plan to play the ball through the middle and a defence that can’t keep goals out to save their lives (or their jobs) is reminiscent of last season’s ‘siege’ mentality.

Nuno failed to keep the side within the Premier League just as he’s failing to keep them in the reckoning for automatic promotion, with the same, cautious, one dimensional game.

Nuno can’t – or won’t – abandon the cautious, slow ponderous style that is drowning the club and frustrating paying supporters.

Which is not what the 55,000 who signed up were expecting this season.

Record transfer fees for the division suggested that we’d be ‘going for it‘ but the absolute lack of ambition, at home, in the last couple of weeks has been the worst part to witness.

Starting without a plan to attack an opponent is something West Ham fans have seen through, as easily as West Brom and Southampton the week before played through the Iron’s token, disorganised defence. Change the players but the style and result remains the same, it seems. And we know where that buck stops.

Much like every season ticket holder, I’ll bet Jarrod Bowen is wondering what on earth he’s signed up for: It certainly wasn’t this disorganised, toothless, spineless procession of mediocrity and the same excuses trotted out week after week. Spare us.

#2103. Celtic handed fresh agony as star who got away rewrites Eredivisie record books

Sizzling Sondre Orjaester tore up the Eredivisie record books on Sunday and handed Celtic an unwanted reminder of the winger who slipped through their grasp.

The Norwegian wide man was the star of the show as FC Twente demolished Excelsior 9-0, chalking up an astonishing FIVE assists in the rout. The remarkable haul is the highest assist tally recorded by a player in a single Eredivisie match this century and underlines the stunning form that has made Orjaester one of the hottest properties in Dutch football.

It's another painful "what if?" moment for Celtic as the Premiership champions continue to search for answers in a difficult campaign.

The Parkhead club kept close tabs on the former Sarpsborg flyer and pushed to land him during the January 2025 transfer window. But despite significant interest, a deal could not be agreed and Orjaester remained in Norway before eventually making the move to Twente.

Read more: Miffed Martin O'Neill bites back in Celtic BBC interview exchange

Celtic instead turned to familiar ground, bringing Jota back to Glasgow in a £10 million deal. However, the Portuguese winger suffered a serious setback when he picked up a long-term injury against Dundee United in April 2025.

That left the Hoops back in the market for reinforcements and, by the close of the summer transfer window, Michel-Ange Balikwisha and Sebastien Tounekti had arrived in a double deal worth around £10m.

Orjaester, meanwhile, was flourishing in the Netherlands.

The 22-year-old previously opened up on why he decided against a switch to the Scottish champions, insisting the style of football on offer elsewhere was a better fit for his development.

Speaking to De Twaalfde Man, he said: "I don't think the type of football played there suits me best.

"The Eredivisie has proven to be a very good platform for young players like me, and there are a lot of technically skilled players there.

"I didn't have much time to think about whether I wanted to go to FC Twente.

"Of course, I knew they were narrowly eliminated in the Europa League last season against Bodø/Glimt. Everyone I spoke to about the club talked about the fans and how Twente played."

While Celtic continue to wrestle with their current issues, Orjaester is producing the sort of numbers that justify the hype which surrounded him. And after rewriting the Eredivisie record books with a five-assist masterclass, the Norwegian has shown exactly why so many believed he could have been a star in green and white.

#2102. West Ham’s £22m Midfielder Appears Untouchable Despite Poor Performances

West Ham have dropped to eighth in the Championship following Saturday’s 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, and the search for answers is becoming increasingly urgent. The Hammers are already losing ground in their attempt to secure an immediate return to the Premier League, with questions understandably being asked about Nuno Espírito Santo and his players.

There is clearly more than one factor behind West Ham’s problems, but one particular selection decision continues to baffle me. Arne Engels appears to have firmly established himself as a Nuno favourite, irrespective of how he performs. The Belgian midfielder remained on the pitch throughout yesterday’s defeat despite, in my opinion, being one of the worst players on it.

As West Ham’s biggest summer signing, costing £22million, Engels was always going to attract scrutiny. That doesn’t mean I have any particular axe to grind with him, but when a player commands that sort of fee and is repeatedly selected ahead of other options, surely we’re entitled to ask whether his performances justify it?

Against West Brom, I thought Engels was truly awful. For large parts of the match, he was the worst player on the pitch.

Arne Engels has struggled in his Championship debut season

His passing was dreadful, he was repeatedly dispossessed by Ousmane Diakité, failed to follow players he was supposed to be marking and generally did an abysmal job with his set-piece deliveries.

In fact, aside from running around a bit, there was barely a facet of his game that he executed particularly well.

In short, Engels endured an absolutely dreadful afternoon, yet somehow managed to remain on the pitch until the final whistle.

While Nuno began withdrawing other players in an effort to fix whatever was broken, Engels appeared impervious to any repercussions.

And this is what I find increasingly difficult to understand.

West Ham have a wealth of options in central midfield, yet Engels appears to be the one player in the engine room guaranteed to start and finish matches.

Don’t get me wrong, I have no problem with managers having favourites, but surely you have to earn that status?

Is Nuno seriously suggesting that Engels is so far ahead of Tomáš Souček, Divine Mukasa, Lewis Orford, Soungoutou Magassa, Edson Álvarez and Mohamadou Kanté that he deserves this preferential treatment?

We have already discussed the extraordinary number of midfield options available to Nuno, yet he seems unable to find a combination that consistently works.

Earlier in the season, there were encouraging signs that Engels and Mukasa could provide the midfield partnership West Ham needed. However, that understanding has hardly developed into the sort of consistency we should expect.

And while players such as Mukasa and Kanté find themselves moved around, substituted or deployed in unfamiliar positions, Engels seems immune to the same treatment.

As an isolated incident, Saturday’s performance would be fine. Players have bad games, and we all understand that.

But Engels seems to have established himself as one of the first names on the team sheet without really earning his stripes.

For me, the jury is still out on the player West Ham paid £22million to sign from Celtic. There is some ability there, and we’ve seen glimpses of what he can do, but that is not the same as consistently performing well enough to justify automatic selection.

I also don’t think the manager is doing him any favours.

Nuno’s reluctance to rotate Engels means there is little opportunity for other midfielders to establish themselves, while the Belgian is being asked to continue playing regardless of his form.

And that brings us back to the wider problem.

West Ham have assembled what should be an excellent collection of Championship midfielders, yet the manager seemingly cannot find a formula that suits any of his smorgasbord of midfield talent.

Engels may be receiving a free pass, but ultimately it is Nuno who keeps handing it to him.

#2101. West Ham Have Not Fallen Below Their Levels – This Is Their Level

West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen has apologised following the Hammers’ 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, admitting the team have fallen well below their usual standards over the past fortnight. However, while I appreciate Jarrod’s honesty, I fundamentally disagree with his assessment of what has gone wrong.

My argument is that West Ham’s performances haven’t suddenly deteriorated over the last two weeks. If anything, the standards have remained remarkably consistent, and the defeats against Southampton and West Brom simply represent the results that many of our earlier performances deserved.

Nuno Espírito Santo’s team have slipped to eighth in the Championship, with their hopes of an immediate Premier League return beginning to look rather less straightforward. But rather than examining two disappointing weeks in isolation, I think we need to look at the warning signs that have been there for considerably longer.

Speaking to the official West Ham website following Saturday’s defeat, Bowen admitted the Hammers had been below their best but had previously found ways to win.

He also acknowledged that the team had fallen below their levels in recent weeks and apologised to supporters.

I appreciate Bowen taking responsibility, particularly after he was one of the few players to emerge from the West Brom defeat with a shred of credit. However, I completely disagree with the suggestion that this represents a sudden collapse in standards.

I think West Ham have simply started getting the results their performances deserve.

Take the 1-0 victory away at Swansea City. It was an excellent result against the league leaders, but West Ham were incredibly poor at the start of that match and hadn’t registered a shot on target after half an hour.

The 6-0 victory against Lincoln City looks fantastic on paper. However, Lincoln were reduced to nine men, and even when they had ten players on the pitch, I thought they were the better team.

It wasn’t until the second half that West Ham really began flexing their muscles against an exhausted side playing with two fewer men.

Queens Park Rangers outplayed us for large periods of our encounter, while everybody remembers quite how dreadful we were during the first half against Millwall.

These weren’t isolated incidents. They were the norm.

To an extent, West Ham have got away with it.

Until a week ago, you could reasonably argue that our league position had been inflated by two 6-0 victories. Those scorelines certainly helped create the impression of a team considerably more dominant than the performances themselves suggested.

The truth is that we’ve already lost three times at home this season.

We might have beaten Wolverhampton Wanderers 4-2, but I thought there were large elements of that match where we were fortunate. Charlton Athletic didn’t find it particularly difficult to beat us either.

Airidas Golambeckis was one of the few who came out of the game without big criticism

In terms of matches played eleven against eleven, I would only really consider the victories against Wrexham and Derby County to have been dominant performances.

That is hardly the form or consistency of a team expecting to secure automatic promotion.

And it is why I find Bowen’s suggestion that West Ham have recently fallen below their usual levels so difficult to accept.

For that to be true, the previous standards would presumably have been considerably higher.

The problems aren’t particularly new. The lack of confidence, cohesion and defensive organisation has been evident for some time.

The difference is that opponents are now making us pay.

There was another part of Bowen’s interview which I found even more concerning.

Discussing West Ham’s habit of starting matches slowly, the captain acknowledged that the problem had been discussed repeatedly within the squad.

He went on to explain that individual players must take responsibility for putting those discussions into practice on the pitch.

And this is where I think the situation becomes particularly worrying.

Because if the players have repeatedly discussed the problem, presumably identified what needs changing and agreed on a plan of action, why does the same thing keep happening?

In many respects, this is the most damning indictment of all.

The players have talked about it. They’ve discussed how to improve. They’ve presumably received instructions from the coaching staff.

Either the plan itself is wrong, in which case serious questions must be asked of Nuno Espírito Santo and his coaching staff, or the plan is perfectly reasonable and the players are incapable of executing it.

Neither possibility is particularly reassuring.

Bowen concluded his interview by making another revealing admission:

On that particular point, I couldn’t agree more.

The talking isn’t working. The tactics aren’t working. The plans aren’t working. And increasingly, the performances on the pitch aren’t working either.

There is only so much discussing, analysing and apologising that can be done before somebody has to produce an actual solution.

West Ham now face consecutive away fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers before the international break, and Bowen has made it clear that the players need to respond with victories.

I certainly wouldn’t question the captain’s commitment. He scored an excellent goal against West Brom and was one of the few players who genuinely looked capable of making something happen.

But his assessment that West Ham have only fallen below their levels during the past fortnight misses what I consider to be the bigger problem.

We’ve been playing like this for much of the season.

The results have simply stopped disguising it.

And if Nuno and his players have already talked through the problems, agreed on solutions and still cannot put them into practice, then I am not entirely sure what there is left to say.

Either the manager’s plan is wrong or the players cannot carry it out.

Whichever it is, West Ham are in a bit of trouble.

#2100. First new Nuno replacement name emerges as disgruntled Hammers point the finger | West Ham News

I was going to start this article with ‘it hasn’t taken long‘ but then I had to back track and begin again. In truth, West Ham have been waiting for Nuno Espirito Santo’s method to catch fire at West Ham ever since his arrival in September 2025. Thirteen months is, by recent standards, an over ‘average’ length of stay for an Irons manager.

Neither of his two predecessors, Julen Lopetegui – less than eight months – and Graham Potter just over eight months, made it to a year in charge before getting the boot.

A manager cannot survive when the fans turn against him and yet Nuno would seem to be on a rock solid foundation thanks to his being Kretinsky’s “continuity candidate’, appointed to see the club through the murky waters post-relegation and while the boardroom was distracted over the Sullivan allegations and then the Staveley takeover.

Plus of course the estimated ten million pounds that’d be required to send the head coach, along with his whole entourage packing.

Ghosts of West Ham future and West Ham past?

That hasn’t stopped names being thrown into the ether – Thomas Frank being the first to appear thanks to talkSPORT yesterday with Jamie O’Hara admitting that the former Spurs, Brentford and Brondby manager would be ‘not a bad shout‘ to replace Nuno.

This, remember, on the back of a story already running that the Hammers leadership have been in discussions with former Wolves manager Rob Edwards.

Will the board act now? Sadly, certainly not.

Six points at this stage of the season is, on paper, just a week’s worth of favourable results and nowhere near enough for the Czech Sphinx to divert his attention from other projects onto the thorny issue of first admitting he was wrong to re-appoint Nuno and then finding a successor.

What West Ham fans will know is that there’s already been a year of fumbling, stuttering management leading up to the Irons’ predicament and another three or six months won’t see any change. Except the chance of automatic promotion will have sailed off down the Swanee in the meantime.

#2099. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#2098. Former West Ham Star ‘Wants’ Manager’s Job as Pressure Mounts on Nuno

After the third defeat of the season at the London stadium, there has been inevitable speculation that Nuno’s job is under threat. Supporters favourite would be Eddie Howe, yet it’s unlikely that the former Newcastle United manager would be interested in the job.

However there is a a former West Ham player reportedly interested in becoming the club’s next head coach should the Hammers decide to part ways with Nuno Espírito Santo in the near future. And it’s not Scott Parker!

Increasing pressure after three home defeats – and six goals conceded in eight days

Current Wales manager Craig Bellamy has privately indicated that he would welcome the opportunity to manage West Ham if the position became available. Bellamy’s former team-mate James Collins recently endorsed the idea during an appearance on TalkSport.

Bellamy has implemented an attractive brand of football with Wales, built around possession, high intensity and an aggressive pressing style. Yet, since taking on the job in 2024, results have been mixed with a 37.5% win ratio during that time. This has not stopped speculation over whether he could one day return to east London in a managerial capacity.

Following Saturday’s 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion, Nuno Espírito Santo acknowledged the scrutiny surrounding his position.

“I am always under pressure, every day,” he said.

Supporters at the London Stadium made their feelings known after the final whistle, with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” directed at the Portuguese Head Coach.

Yet despite the clubs current position in eighth place, Nuno Espírito Santo is expected to be given more time. Daniel Kretinsky continues to support the Portuguese coach, although both parties understand the pressure that comes with football management.

For now, Bellamy’s interest appears to be one for the future rather than the present. Nuno still retains the backing of the club’s hierarchy, but football can change quickly and results will ultimately determine his fate.

Should a managerial vacancy arise down the line, Bellamy’s connection to West Ham and his exciting coaching philosophy could make him a name worth watching.

#2097. The curious tale of Virgil van Dijk and Dan Burn

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Exactly two weeks ago I wrote an article about Dan Burn and Virgil vak Dijk.

Newcastle United had lost 1-0 at home to Aston Villa on the Saturday.

That article I did on Monday 19 October 2026 was sparked by seeing another piece on The Mag that morning, ‘Newcastle United striker problem’ by Oden Hudson: ‘Let’s start with the most obvious sign that the club has an issue in forward areas – we ended the [Aston Villa] game with Dan Burn at striker. A comical decision that not even the most rogue Football Manager player would dare consider, this is an abhorrently dreadful and comical sign that we have truly failed to address our issues up top over the summer.’

This has become a huge topic of conversation for many fans and indeed those in the media. Dan Burn playing up front for Newcastle United against Aston Villa.

This used by numerous people after the Villa match as final ‘proof’ of how bad things are at NUFC. Along the lines of  ‘proof’ of how clueless Matthias Jaissle, how rubbish the Newcastle United team is, how terrible the transfer policy is, and so on.

The way that writer and others were going on, you would have though Matthias Jaissle had played Dan Burn as a striker from the start of that Aston Villa match.

The reality was that Dan Burn came on in the 90th minute for Joelinton, who was knackered after starting his first competitive game in more than five months. Having trailed at the break, Newcastle United were the better team in the second half but struggled to break down an Aston Villa defence that was now set. Defending deep, Villa were very difficult to play through, whilst crosses into the box were getting zero joy as Villa’s tall defenders headed them all away, or Suzuki dealt with them,  we could all see United were getting nowhere as added time approached.

So Matthias Jaissle throwing Dan Burn on for the added time minutes in the hope he might cause a bit of chaos in the Villa penalty area, win the odd header that the rest of the United players had failed to do. It almost worked as well a couple of promising situations and one moment in particular, where if the ball had fallen more kindly then a Newcastle player (can’t remember who) would have had a huge clear chance from only seven or eight yards or so.

I couldn’t see anything wrong with doing that, chucking Dan Burn up front for the last few minutes. I didn’t have a problem with it. What I really did have a problem with was those Newcastle United fans and some in the media making out that this was the most ridiculous thing in the world and no other manager or team had ever done such a thing in the history of the game.

The fact is that countless other managers had done the same AND continue to do the same.

I quoted the example of Harry Maguire at Manchester United, he has been similarly used in the past as a last chance resort up front when Man U have been desperate for a goal. Indeed, ahead of the World Cup finals, a big debate was whether Thomas Tuchel should take Dan Burn or Harry Maguire. Neither were seen as going to be starting the England games but the key thing the media all agreed on was they could be brought on late in matches to help defend a lead, or to be thrown up front if they were desperate for a goal late on and struggling to create chances. Not playing as a striker for a long time but in the very final stages hanging around up front and a chance to try something different, win a key header maybe, cause some chaos.

My main quoted example two weeks ago though was Virgil van Dijk, I had seen him sent up front late on in countless Liverpool matches. With absolutely zero ridicule aimed at Jurgen Klopp or Arne Slot for doing so.

Surprise surprise, yesterday I saw relatively long before the final whistle at Anfield, Virgil van Dijk sent up front to try and salvage something as they trailed Arsenal. In the Sky Sports commentary this was seen as perfectly valid and an obvious thing to do to try something different, a tall central defender playing up front to try and get on the end of some crosses and long balls. Liverpool still didn’t manage an effort on target all match and lost the game BUT nothing negative has been said at all by anybody in the media or elsewhere, regarding this tactic of employing Virgil van Dijk as an emergency striker late on.

I think it is all a bit pathetic the way that certain journalists went on about Dan Burn playing those few minutes up front in the Villa defeat, a cowardly and not valid reason for having a go at Matthias Jaissle and Newcastle United generally.

Even worse the clueless Newcastle United fans doing the same, desperate to have a go at the new NUFC Head Coach by any means possible.

There are valid questions to be asked and debated on both Matthias Jaissle and Newcastle United generally. However, using that Dan Burn ‘striker’ thing as a stick to beat him and the club with was beyond embarrassing.

#2096. “Who else is standing up?” – Report claims players no longer fighting for Nuno | West Ham News

As the third goal went in yesterday, shoulders visibly sank around the players on the pitch as the home fans booed their efforts and the apparent ease in which second division sides are able to give West Ham the run around.

This, supposedly the strongest team in the Championship being humbled by a hard working West Brom after Southampton made the Irons look very ordinary seven days before.

It might not yet have reached the full-on crisis of a manager having irrevocably lost his dressing room, but West Ham fan and journalist Roshane Thomas has pinpointed what he sees as a squad rapidly losing investment in their manager’s success.

A precursor to disaster if Nuno’s squad no longer buy in to his ability to turn around their dismal record of conceding goals.

Report claims Bowen alone is invested in fighting for his manager

Writing in the NYTimes, Thomas pulls no punches with his article title:

“Nuno’s side remain horribly reliant upon Jarrod Bowen. He scored the equaliser against West Brom, but struggled to inspire another comeback once the visitors had restored their lead.

The winger had levelled matters up in the recent 1-1 draw against Queens Park Rangers, prompting the stadium announcer to boom: “Who else?” in recognition of his importance.

Konstantinos Mavropanos is sidelined with a knee injury, while Mohamadou Kante, Divine Mukasa and Tomas Soucek have helped ease the offensive burden on Bowen. But Engels, Manor Solomon, Taty Castellanos and Pablo have not followed suit. Joel Piroe, a proven goalscorer in the Championship, has been limited to substitute appearances.”

Many have highlighted the dizzying array of combinations Nuno has used for his starting eleven – not once has he fielded the same eleven names on the team sheet in consecutive fixtures, unlike 17 of his Championship competitors – yet his intransigence over failing goal keeper Mads Hermansen’s place in the side, along with a refusal to bring back outcasts Alvarez and Magassa reeks of favouritism over pragmatism.

Which tells me what West Ham are getting from Nuno is not what is needed: Sticking to favourites, ignoring outcasts and endless fiddling around with starting players out of position is one easy way to test the patience of players in the dressing room.

As Thomas clearly points out. Once that happens, the exit door cannot be far away. The next two games ahead of the break are crucial for Nuno – and for the club.

#2095. Régis Le Bris gets official Sunderland vote of confidence to keep on doing great job

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It has now been revealed that Régis Le Bris has been told by Sunderland he has their full support and will continue in the job.

It looked like the writing was on the wall when rock bottom Sunderland were outplayed and outclassed by second bottom Coventry City on Saturday, lucky to only lose 3-1. The Sky Blues now four points clear of hapless Sunderland.

However, Sky Sports report that they have had official confirmation that Régis Le Bris has been informed his job is safe.

Keith Downie covers Sunderland and Newcastle United for Sky Sports and he states: “Régis Le Bris’ position as Sunderland Head Coach is safe and he continues to have the full support and confidence of Sunderland’s hierarchy. The Frenchman remains central to Sunderland plans and ambitions, despite the club sitting bottom of the Premier League table. The belief within the club is the 50-year-old will turn things around.”

Sunderland have lost five and drawn one of their last six Premier League matches and their late (no) consolation goal on Saturday came after more than six hours of league football without scoring.

Sunderland have now picked up only two points from their last possible 21 and their only Premier League victory over the season was back in August, a lucky late 1-0 home win over Fulham.

The man from Sky Sports adding about what they have heard from inside Sunderland AFC: “There is an internal recognition that recent Premier League results have been disappointing and the club understand current frustrations felt by supporters. The club believe stability, collective responsibility and a united approach is the way forward for Sunderland as they look to achieve their ambitions….”

Yes, Régis Le Bris is doing a great job at Sunderland and hopefully they will keep faith with him as they continue to lose many more matches.

After losing so convincingly to the club that was second bottom, in the Premier League Sunderland now face Chelsea (home), Aston Villa (away), Spurs (home) and Liverpool (away). Before then heading to St James’ Park on Sunday 6 December to face Newcastle United. Whether Régis Le Bris will still have by that point the full backing of the Sunderland hierarchy remains to be seen… 🎙️ THE MAG PODCAST THE NEW MAG POD IS LIVE! #2094. Nuno Has Had Long Enough – West Ham Need a Change

I’ve seen enough. For me, Nuno Espírito Santo’s time as West Ham manager should be up.

I’ve had nearly 24 hours to reflect on the dreadful 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, and without the immediate anger and frustration of the final whistle, my opinion hasn’t changed. If anything, I’m even more convinced that Nuno isn’t the man to take West Ham forward.

This isn’t simply a reaction to one bad result or even two consecutive defeats. It’s the culmination of more than a year of watching a manager who still doesn’t appear to know his best team, his preferred formation or how to get the best out of the attacking players at his disposal.

The football has become stale, the players look unmotivated and, perhaps most worrying of all, I’m struggling to see any genuine improvement.

Jarrod Bowen says words are no longer enough, and I completely agree. But when I look back at our performances throughout the season, I’m not convinced these last two defeats represent some sudden collapse in standards. I think the problems have been there for quite some time.

In my latest video, I explain why I’ve finally lost faith in Nuno, why I don’t believe this is an overreaction and why West Ham need to act before our promotion ambitions suffer any further damage.

I’m also concerned about the empty seats, the growing apathy amongst supporters and the fact that watching West Ham has become such a chore.

I know plenty of supporters will disagree with me, and that’s absolutely fine. We all want West Ham to succeed.

But for me, the time has come for a change.

Nuno has had long enough. West Ham need to move on.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2092. Nuno gets a huge slice of positive news ahead of must-win Cardiff City encounter | West Ham News

Under fire Nuno Espírito Santo has a couple of games coming up that are in, in effect, must-win if West Ham are to get back on track with their promotion push and keep up with league leaders Middlesborough.

Next weekend the Irons travel north west to take on Blackburn Rovers after a Wednesday night trip in three days’ time to Cardiff City’s home for a crucial encounter under the lights.

Names are already being thrown around was possible successors should Nuno falter in the last two games heading into the two week international break.

Lose both ties that lie ahead and the Portuguese will surely be given his marching orders by West Ham’s board, who are reluctant to part ways with their chosen manager but cannot be immune to the dissatisfaction being voiced from just about every quarter following yesterday’s dèbacle.

Walker Peters is unlikely to make Wednesday night’s game but opponents Cardiff face much greater challenges

Right on time, however, there’s some good news for Nuno: Wednesday’s opponents are in something of a major injury crisis, as revealed by walesonline today:

Cardiff City’s injury crisis has deepened ahead of West Ham’s visit, with Brian Barry-Murphy facing mounting selection headaches and fresh concerns”

The Bluebirds’ defensive choices look particularly bleak, with Will Fish suffering a hamstring injury and Perry Ng also struggling, whilst Alex Robertson with an Achilles problem and Krystian Bielik are both expected to be absent.

Other players confirmed unavailable include Gabriel Osho due to suspension, as well as Dylan Lawlor and Calum Chambers, who are both sidelined through injury.

West Ham, conversely, might just escape with Kyle Walker Peters the only absentee –  if Dinos Mavropanos continues his near miraculous recovery from last weekend’s knee injury.

Which might just give West Ham the edge they need to go and grab three points and put the horrors of the last week – and the uncertainty over Nuno’s future – behind them.

Losing again doesn’t bear thinking about.

#2091. Newcastle United v Everton preview ahead of tonight’s St James’ Park match

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Welcome to the Newcastle United v Everton preview.

Newcastle look for revenge against the Toffees on Monday night as the two clubs face-off for the second time in just five days.

The blues got the better of United first time around when dumping the 2025 champions out of the League Cup and the Toon will be desperate to get their season back on track following such disappointment.

Three points for either side would have them in the top seven of the Premier League. The match will once again take place on live TV and a global audience will be waiting to see if the Toon can build on their win over Crystal Palace last weekend, as we look to put together a run of form ahead of the busy Christmas period that can make or break a season.

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their last six league matches. Wins have come against Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Bournemouth despite going 2-0 down. Defeats away to Leeds and Coventry saw the Toon get battered 4-1 on both occasions whereas Villa also took three points from St James Park in our last home match. The Toon have scored eight goals in these six matches but conceded a whopping twelve. The seven points gained has us twelfth in the league but a win would see us in seventh place.

Everton have only won one of their last six matches and have lost their last two in a row, drawing the other three. They beat Ipswich 1-0, drew with Tottenham, Man United and Hull and lost to both Chelsea and Arsenal. They’ve scored five goals in these six matches and conceded eight. A win on Monday would see them leapfrog the Toon and rocket seven places up the league. The Toffees were unbeaten in all competitions before the last two league matches so will be determined to alleviate this slump before it sees them slide towards a relegation scrap.

A quirk of the fixture list saw the two sides play each other in their last match having been drawn together at the Hill Dickinson stadium in the League Cup. Despite a promising start for United, this was ultimately a night to forget. Everton survived some early pressure before taking a two-goal lead into halftime. A number of substitutions saw the Toon attempt to wrest some momentum back from the Toffees. Any romantic notion of a famous comeback however was dispelled in the sixty-ninth minute when Everton scored again to take a three-goal advantage. There was still time for Dan Burn to net a late consolation but it was too little, too late as Everton dashed out Wembley dreams.

Newcastle haven’t beaten Everton in their last three visits to St James’ Park.

The Toon have lost only once in five home matches in all competitions this season.

NUFC have scored thirteen goals in their past eight home matches against Everton.

The 2007/08 season had very few highlights under Sam Allardyce who was thankfully shown the door in January. Big Sam had overseen only seven Premier League victories in twenty-one matches at the Toon. The Toffees visited St James’ Park in early October and the two sides played out a quite incredible five-goal thriller. Newcastle were the better team in the first half but were wasteful in front of goal as misses from Martins, N’Zogbia and Geremi looked to ensure that the teams were to go into the half-time break goalless. Thankfully Nicky Butt volleyed home at the Leazes End just before the interval to give the Toon the initiative. Anyone thinking this would mean NUFC would have things all their own way however were to have another thing coming when Johnson equalised just a few minutes into the second half to place the tie on a knife edge. An end-to-end second forty-five saw both sides push for a winner without really looking like they believed it possible until late substitutes were to make the difference. With just five minutes left, Emre picked up the ball outside of the area and unleashed an absolute rocket into the bottom corner from fully twenty-five yards out. A few minutes later, the Turkish midfielder turned provider when floating a freekick into the danger zone for Michael Owen to nod a header in off the bar and seal the destination of the points. There was still time for a wicked deflection to completely bamboozle Shay Given and end up in the back of the net but this was followed by the final whistle as United were able to celebrate three memorable points. Newcastle 3-2 Everton.

Antony Gordon came through the youth system at Everton having joined their academy at eleven years old. He made his debut in the Europa League aged just sixteen and spent six years at the Toffees. He played sixty-five league matches and scored seven goals over a six year period. He joined Newcastle in January 2023 under difficult circumstances following a well-publicised incident where he was harassed by supporters when leaving the stadium following a 0-0 draw with Southampton. He’d go on to enjoy an eventful three and half years at St James Park as NUFC qualified twice for the Champions League and he helped United to Wembley for the 2025 League Cup final, finally breaking a long-standing trophy duck in 2025. The 2025 League Cup would show both the good and bad of Anthony Gordon, scoring crucial goals in both legs of a semi-final success but being suspended for the final for a needless sending off just a few weeks later, meaning he missed out on playing in the greatest game of our recent history. He signed for Barcelona for over sixty-nine million pounds a few months back having scored twenty-four league goals in one-hundred-and-eleven appearances.

Paul Gascoigne was arguably one of the most naturally talented players to have ever come out of our country. Born in Gateshead, he made his debut for the Toon in 1985 and scored twenty-five goals in one-hundred appearances before signing for Tottenham in 1988. A million words could be written about ‘Gazza’ both on and off the pitch, books can and have been written about such an enigmatic figure. His story is eventful, intriguing, funny and tragic in equal measure. He played for Everton from 2000-2002 and scored a single goal in thirty-two league matches.

David Ginola was perhaps one of the most exciting players ever to represent NUFC in the Premier League era. Highlights of his two years on Tyneside include superb goals against Sheffield Wednesday, Man United and Ferencvaros, whilst equally memorable was his ability to whip the ball into the box loading the bullets for Sir Les and then Shearer to fire home. Tragically sold to Spurs by Kenny Dalglish in the same summer that Ferdinand also went to White Hart Lane, Ginola became something of a pantomime villain when playing against NUFC for the remainder of his career. Thankfully his retirement has seen a thawing in relations and he’s rightly remembered by Toon fans as a modern day legend. He played for Everton in 2002 but made only five league appearances for the Toffees.

Matthias Jaissle after a 3-1 defeat away at Everton in the League Cup: “Shocking and frustrating but if you just see the bigger picture, we did well in many aspects of the game. We of course are disappointed with the result, it’s also a bit shocking at the moment because overall the game was not that bad, but it’s the story of the season so far, that in situations where it really counts we lack the clinical approach to solve the situations. Just thinking about the first goal, it’s no risk zone, we clear the ball and nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later we concede a goal out of nothing. The second one is also frustrating in my point of view, we deserved to have a penalty then we miss in a transition to defend our own box which again is difficult to accept. We have clear rules then how to behave. We need to learn quickly. For me it’s about being mature in the situations, more clinical to solve the situations and not allowing almost a gift for the opposition to score. It feels like the opposition is not giving us these gifts at the moment so we need to avoid that.”

David Moyes after a 3-1 win against Newcastle United: “I thought it was a tough game. Newcastle had moments in the game but I think the Premier League is a bit like this at the moment. I think the games are quite close. You could be defending for twenty minutes and then you might be better for another twenty minutes. I think the games are very tight. Obviously we got the goals at good times, certainly the third goal sort of killed the game off at that time when Newcastle were probably better at the start of the second half.”

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank

Thursday night was hugely disappointing for everyone concerned with NUFC for a number of reasons. The carrot of a match against League Two Fleetwood Town for a place in the cup semi-final was carelessly tossed away. That’s gone now and it’s important we build up a head of steam in the Premier League having got things back on track last weekend with a win over Crystal Palace. Newcastle need revenge against Everton and I fancy us to get it with two early goals putting the match to bed in the first half. Newcastle 2-0 Everton.

#2090. Liverpool boss in astonishing admission - I will urge my players to dive

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he will urge his players to dive in future after Alexander Isak was refused a penalty in Sunday’s 1-0 loss to Arsenal.

The Liverpool striker’s shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber as he leapt to reach a cross into the box during the first half of the Premier League encounter at Anfield.

Isak did not go to ground and referee Andy Madley gave nothing. VAR Stuart Attwell also saw no reason to overturn the decision.

Asked if players should go down, Iraola said: “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them, go down, because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

Read more: ‘Emotional’ Marink Reedijk enjoys post-match scenes as Hibernian book final spot

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like, no, you are all the time going down.

“But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

He added in a BBC interview: “The answer is you have to dive. If you don’t dive they are not going to call it.”

The incident occurred soon after Arsenal had taken the lead in the 16th minute as Kai Havertz benefited from an Alisson Becker error.

Liverpool went on to dominate for large spells but could not break Arsenal’s resilience.

Florian Wirtz did hit the bar from a free-kick and Cody Gakpo also had a penalty appeal turned down after a tussle with Christos Tzolis but Iraola was less concerned about that decision.

He said: “The Gakpo one, I think it’s a sustained holding but I understand their argument and I think they are right that they say the ball was too long and Cody wouldn’t have arrived to the ball.

“I think we have to blame the start of the game. Until we conceded the goal, (we were not) at the level of the rest of the game. But from 1-0, I loved the reaction of the team.”

Arsenal’s victory was their first at Anfield in the league for 14 years and took them to the top of the table.

Manager Mikel Arteta said the champions were motivated by a desire to bounce back from their shock Carabao Cup loss to League Two Fleetwood in midweek.

Arteta said: “It has been such a long time without having this winning feeling here.

“We are extremely proud of the team and the players and what everyone has done, especially in the conditions in which we arrived to this game – the defeat against Fleetwood looks the end of the world, but then you have to pick yourself up.

“How the hell can you go out of the cup when you shoot 27 times and have the chances we had against a team who had one shot on target? Then you look so silly but I had the feeling now was the moment.”

#2089. Defender lifts the lid on West Ham dressing room chaos | West Ham News

West Ham United’s dressing room must have felt as if it has been under siege for most of the last three years, with a string of managerial misfires and sackings, disruptive and outright ‘want  – away’ stars and two relegation battles fought in succession.

On top, of course the ‘BS out’ fan protests further contributed to the controversy surrounding the club, which peaked with relegation being confirmed last May  – and then the historic allegations forcing Chairman David Sullivan to quit just weeks after Vice Chair Karren Brady’s resignation.

Former Hammers defender Emerson has described the way in which the bombshell that was the  Lucas Paquetá inquiry catapulted the whole club into chaos, not long after the idyllic summer of ‘2023 – where it has seemingly remained ever since.

According to sportwitness.co.uk, Paquetá’s fellow countryman Emerson reckoned the whole Hammers dressing room was taken by surprise and plunged into controversy:

“The midfielder openly admitted that the case had taken a severe strain on his mental health. Palmieri now admits that it was not easy for everyone else at West Ham either…

Fellow countrymen Emerson Palmieri and Lucas Paqueta back in happier times before the storms broke in the Irons’ dressing room and beyond

“It was very tough because it caught us all by surprise..

I was taken aback when these kinds of allegations started to surface. And then we saw the scale it reached. He was facing the possibility of a suspension—or even a lifetime ban from football. He was deeply saddened by everything that was being linked to his name.”

Few fans perhaps appreciate the upset on the whole West Ham team and the dressing room created by the two-year long FA inquiry.

Certainly Lucas Paquetá never reached the heights of his first season as a Hammer after living with the spectre of a lifetime ban hanging over his head for years.

The player lost his dream move to Manchester City – and perhaps more importantly West Ham United were forced to try and maintain their Premier League standing whilst the allegations and the FA inquiry rolled over their heads like some impending thunderstorm.

In hindsight, it is little wonder that relegation resulted last May after the litany of crises involving the players, the club and its owners pretty much ever since that idyllic June day in 2023.

#2088. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

INS:Illan Meslier from Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis from Club Brugge, £34mBruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, £75m

Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

OUTS:Leandro Trossard to Besiktas, £18mJakub Kiwior to Porto, £15m

August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4August 5-  Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3Today- Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (Emirates Cup)August 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield)

🚨 STARTING XI VS ARSENAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/Wk6QPOGDnW

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️🧱 Gabriel at the back©️ Odegaard skippers the side😤 Gyokeres leads the line More pre-season minutes in the tank - let's do this, Gunners ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/FQwOjCDAje

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.
