#2086. Championship striker pinpoints Hammers’ problem and offers hope for week ahead | West Ham News

Amongst the many voices raised over Nuno’s travails at West Ham following two consecutive home defeats, some opinions  deserve more consideration than others.

One former Championship player who knows only too well the challenges faced by teams struggling to compete in this, the toughest of the English leagues, has added to the growing suggestion that West Ham’s home form is suspect due to the weight of home expectation.

Important to remember that all three of the Irons’ defeats this season have come in front of an increasingly vocal, critical home fan base at London Stadium, and former Hull city and Peterborough striker Aaron McLean is certain it’s all down to the pressures of playing at home.

Writing for the bbc.co.uk after witnessing the Hammers’ second capitulation in two consecutive home games, McLean suggests:

“West Ham just don’t seem to be handling the pressure.

The fanbase is very split in terms of whether they want Nuno Espirito Santo in charge but the thing you have to do when playing for West Ham in front of 60,000 fans is put in a performance and if you’re in the Championship, you have to win.

BBC pundit McLean believes the Hammers squad aren’t coping with the pressure of playing in front of their own, demanding fan base at home.

“When you have a lovely stadium and playing surface, teams want to go there and enjoy it.

If you make your home ground a fortress, that can work for you but at the moment, the London Stadium is not a fortress and teams are going there and enjoying the experience, which is the total opposite of what West Ham need.”

As we wrote last week, the very weight of expectation appears to be hanging heavily around the players’ necks at present. If that is the case then the up and coming away fixtures at Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers this week will carry no such difficulties – merely unending vocal support from a travelling support that simply sings its heart out – whatever the match situation.

Just what Nuno’s men need right now. A couple of away days before the international break with the chance to get back to winning ways, without the weight of the world on their shoulders. Dealing with the pressure at home is another problem altogether.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

What you didn’t add Martin, was he was asked if he (Aaron Maclean ) if he backed Nuno to succeed and he said yes he did. Well us West Ham fans know what a disaster Nuno is.

I must admit disagree with the comment ‘if in the Championship you have to win’ and all this talk about we should be top of the table. Yes, we have a good squad but we have not played all the teams in the table at least once to place ourselves, so we are completely ignoring their qualities.

The team is not playing well. Team manager needs to adapt style of play to his players abilities, stop chopping and changing so team get to know each other’s style of play etc., etc., … we all have our ideas; just saying ‘must win’ is simply meaningless.

‘Automatic promotion’ & expecting Championship WHU to be able to recruit PL standard players to the club, same illusion, words which have been just as meaningless.

Constantly putting the cart before the horse.

fan base, positivity, right attitude are niceties, valuable extras. Get your team playing consistently good football, stop making managerial errors, stand up for your players off pitch, the rest will follow including player attitudes, fan base, positivity,…

Change training routines, coaching objectives, play a 45 min game against U21s to model style of football that good teams play in Championship.. I don’t know, but THINK! You the coaches are doing a lot of things wrong and the result is on the pitch – fix them..

Everyone is table watching amongst the pundits but WHU fans know that the manager is often his worst enemy. If team beat Cardiff and we go up in the table, it means little. So style of play does count.

Everything else such as player attitude, fanbase, excitement comes after, not before.

50,000 fans roaring you on…. Our players should be relishing it yet they lack the bravery to perform.

Instead our opponents are the ones showing the bravery. It’s a state of mind which our coach seems unable to develop and instil with this squad.

#2085. Duo escape criticism after West Ham slow start shocker against Baggies | West Ham News

Two names seemed – deservedly – absent from the long list of players singled out for culpability amongst the anger and consternation felt across fan channels and the wider football media this weekend, as pre-season favourites West Ham slumped to their third home defeat of the season.

Jarrod Bowen, without saying, put in a shift and dragged the Hammers back once with a trademark run and low shot: But two of West Ham’s youngsters both put in solid shifts, despite the result, and are deserving of warmer words than the rest of the starting line up.

West Ham’s Edvin Austbø – another one who escaped criticism amidst a crap team performance

Playing alongside the tentative Maximilian Kilman would tax the abilities of any decent centre half and it is vital for West Ham’s future that he doesn’t find himself banished back to the u21’s after one start and a result that reflects badly on the whole team.

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Matthias Jaissle has issued a statement of intent ahead of the Everton match tonight..

The game an 8pm kick-off at St James’ Park.

Newcastle United looking to bounce back from Thursday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Everton.

Though at the same time follow up their last Premier League game, a 2-0 win at Crystal Palace.

Ahead of this Everton challenge tonight, Matthias Jaissle declaring: “”I must acknowledge the disappointment we all felt following Thursday night’s Carabao Cup game at Everton, especially with such an incredible away following of nearly 8,000 supporters. There is no time to feel sorry for ourselves and make excuses – we have to learn quickly, understand what went wrong and where we need to be better, and then make sure we put it into action with a response on the pitch tonight.”

Newcastle United will go seventh top if winning against Everton.

The German Head Coach telling Newcastle United fans: “We showed our intent with the number of chances created and, after making a really promising start to the game on Thursday, I felt like we were in a strong position to build on the win at Crystal Palace. Unfortunately, as we have experienced this season already, we allowed the opposition some good opportunities that could have been prevented and ultimately they punished us. That is the nature of football at this level and over the weekend at the training ground we have been really focused on identifying and working on the areas we need to improve.”

Matthias Jaissle stating: “I have said many times already that we are going through a period of transition and we fully expect to experience ups and downs this season, as the last week has shown. What’s vital after nights like Thursday is that we all stick together, in the same way that we all celebrate together and enjoy the moment after wins like Crystal Palace. I admit that sometimes it is easier said than done, but it is important that we don’t get too high after a win and we don’t get too low after a defeat. The defeats will test our character and they will hurt in the short term, but we need to show the right mentality to respond in a positive way and remain focused on the bigger picture. After a defeat you want the next game to come as soon as possible to try and put things right. Thankfully we have that opportunity tonight against the same opposition as Thursday.”

#2083. The Strange Pattern Behind Every Major West Ham Managerial Appointment

A social media post doing the rounds over the weekend has sparked an interesting debate among West Ham supporters, highlighting what some see as a recurring theme in the club’s managerial appointments under David Sullivan and the late David Gold.

The post lists a succession of West Ham managers and jokingly categorises them by their playing positions:

The less charitable description attached to Avram Grant is perhaps best left where it belongs, on social media. He actually never played professional football!

While the observation is obviously tongue-in-cheek, it does raise an intriguing point. Since Sullivan and Gold took control of West Ham in 2010, the club has overwhelmingly turned to former defenders and goalkeepers when appointing managers.

Defenders and goalkeepers are often associated with organisation, structure and caution. Many of the managers West Ham have appointed during the ownership era have certainly prioritised defensive solidity first and attacking football second.

Bilic – one in a long line of defenders or ‘keepers appointed as West Ham Manager

That said, West Ham have hardly looked defensively secure under Nuno this season, and many teams have taken full advantage of those weaknesses.

Allardyce built his reputation on pragmatism. Moyes delivered the most successful period of the modern era through discipline, shape and resilience. Even Pellegrini, despite his reputation for attacking football at Manchester City, spent much of his West Ham spell battling to find defensive balance.

The goalkeeper connection is perhaps even more interesting. Both Lopetegui and Nuno Espírito Santo were former keepers, with each enjoying success elsewhere before taking on the challenge in east London.

Of course, there is no evidence that Sullivan sat down with a shortlist and immediately crossed off every former midfielder or striker. Football management success rarely comes down to the position someone played during their career.

After all, some of the Premier League’s most successful modern managers have come from every area of the pitch.

Yet supporters often look for patterns when results are poor, and West Ham’s recent struggles have inevitably led to fresh examination of decision-making at boardroom level.

Whether the theory is meaningful or merely an amusing statistical quirk, one thing is certain, Hammers fans would probably care far less about a manager’s former position if the current team was climbing the Championship table.

Sometimes football’s strangest observations turn out to be nothing more than coincidence. This may well be one of them. But it is the sort of coincidence that will get supporters talking.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

What do you expect when you have unambitious, dullard, embarrassing, two bob, cheapo, gobby owners; you get tinpot appointments.

Loser managers that are unemployed and no-one else wants.

Even the reappointment of Moyes was an embarrassing and two bob appointment at the time as he’d been jobless since his first stint with us.

It was pure chance and an absolute fluke that he did well for us.

Pellegrini was the only ambitious appointment, and even that was only forced due to rioting from our supporters due to the owners lies and lack of ambition.

The sooner David Sullivan and his sons have no involvement in the club, the better.

He doesn’t look in the best of health, and he won’t be here forever.

I can think of something else which all those former and present West Ham managers might have in common. They were all unemployed and probably had all been sacked!

Strange how many of them were unable to see our defensive frailties over the years, although when Stuart Pearce was employed as first team coach we did look much more solid at the back.

the other thing that they have in common, with the exception of Moyes is they’re all absolute rubbish. ( being nice).

#2081. If West Ham Cannot Sack Nuno – Then He Must Make These Immediate Changes

Calls for West Ham United manager Nuno Espírito Santo to be sacked are growing louder following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion. The Hammers have dropped to eighth in the Championship, and supporters are understandably questioning whether the Portuguese coach is capable of leading the club back to the Premier League.

I certainly fall squarely into the camp of people who don’t believe Nuno can either motivate his players or outsmart many of his rival Championship managers. The football has become stale, the team looks disjointed and there is precious little evidence of a manager getting the best out of what should be a very competitive squad.

But if we’re absolutely honest with ourselves, I suspect most West Ham supporters would acknowledge that Nuno is nowhere near being sacked. So rather than simply demanding his removal, perhaps the more useful question is what he can actually change to get this team playing better.

There are several reasons why I suspect Espírito Santo will remain in charge for the foreseeable future.

Firstly, West Ham are still in a state of flux regarding the club’s ownership structure. Until the proposed changes involving Vanessa Gold’s shareholding are completed and the i’s are dotted and t’s crossed, there remains uncertainty about precisely who will be making the biggest decisions.

Secondly, despite bringing in the best part of £200million through summer player sales, there are questions about how much money the club actually has available. Whether West Ham would be willing or able to fund another managerial dismissal and appointment is unclear.

And thirdly, if Daniel Křetínský is indeed calling the shots, Nuno is very much the manager he backed to lead the club through this Championship campaign.

Which leaves us with a rather uncomfortable situation. A manager whose football is becoming increasingly difficult to defend, but who may nevertheless be extremely secure in his job.

The first thing I’d change is the defence.

Nuno needs to abandon the experiment of playing Morato at left-back and select a proper full-back in that position.

I appreciate that Morato has performed reasonably well at times, and his versatility has been useful. But ultimately he’s a central defender, and I don’t believe the arrangement is helping West Ham develop a balanced team.

Whether Nuno selects Adama Boiro or Ollie Scarles doesn’t particularly matter to me at this stage.

We need better balance, more natural movement down the left and defenders playing in positions they understand.

As I’ve said previously, Arne Engels appears to be guaranteed a game irrespective of how he performs. Meanwhile, Nuno seems to believe he can win the Championship without consistently selecting a recognised defensive midfielder.

West Ham have a wealth of options in central midfield, yet we repeatedly find ourselves overrun, unable to retain possession and exposed whenever opponents break forward.

For that reason, I think it’s probably time to change the midfield completely.

I’d be tempted to give Lewis Orford another opportunity alongside either Edson Álvarez or Soungoutou Magassa.

Both Álvarez and Magassa offer the possibility of greater defensive protection, something West Ham have been desperately lacking.

And with a more secure base behind him, Divine Mukasa could finally be deployed in his best position as a number ten.

He’s a wonderfully gifted young footballer, but we’re wasting too much of his ability by asking him to drop deep and collect possession from the centre-backs.

Get him further up the pitch, give him some protection behind him and let him start opening up opposition defences.

Between the sticks, Mads Hermansen hasn’t exactly covered himself in glory.

I’m not suggesting every goal West Ham concede is his fault, because the defending in front of him has frequently been dreadful.

But when a team is struggling this badly, nobody should be guaranteed their place simply because they’ve been selected regularly.

Nuno has an ex PCG goalkeeper in Alphonse Areola at his disposal… surely it’s worth a try?

Which brings us to the striking department.

Leading up to the Southampton game, plenty of people were keen to repeat the fallacy that West Ham couldn’t win football matches without Pablo.

It’s worth remembering that Pablo didn’t start the Hammers’ 6-0 victory against Wrexham, which I consider our most convincing performance of the season.

And following back-to-back defeats in which the £23million striker started both matches, I suspect that particular myth has been exposed to all but his most vociferous supporters.

I don’t question Pablo’s effort. He works hard, puts himself about and certainly isn’t afraid of making a tackle.

Unfortunately, those qualities alone don’t make somebody an effective Championship striker.

For that reason, I’d be inclined to give Joël Piroe, our only proven Championship goalscorer among the recognised centre-forwards, a proper opportunity to establish himself.

He hasn’t been given anything resembling a consistent run in the side, and I struggle to understand how Nuno can properly assess his options without giving him one.

I’m not suggesting Piroe is guaranteed to solve our problems.

Of course, all these changes will count for very little unless Nuno can find a way to motivate his players.

I have little doubt that West Ham possess a number of talented footballers, many of whom I suspect would look considerably better under different coaches.

Once the players cross that white line, tactics, organisation and selection become equally important.

And that is where Nuno continues to let himself down.

Whether any of my suggestions would make a significant difference, I genuinely don’t know.

But I do know that repeating the same errors time and again isn’t going to get West Ham back into contention for automatic promotion.

The players who have consistently underperformed need to be dropped, and those who haven’t had much of an opportunity deserve a chance.

We have enough players in this squad to try something different.

And frankly, that’s probably the best we can hope for at the moment.

Because as much as some West Ham supporters might wish for Nuno Espírito Santo’s removal, I suspect he’s currently extremely secure in his job.

Which means if West Ham are going to improve, the manager who created many of these problems is probably going to have to be the one who solves them.

#2080. Ally McCoist left in stitches as Derek McInnes makes Rangers admission on-air

Rangers hero Ally McCoist was left in stitches as Derek McInnes issued an on-air one-liner over his start to life as Rangers manager.

The Ibrox hero couldn't contain his laughter as the Rangers boss admitted he faced a rocky opening to his tenure in Govan.

Rangers had exited the Europa League to Jagiellonia Bialystok, then the Conference League qualifiers to Jablonec before a draw and defeat in their opening two league matches.

However, since then Rangers have gone on a run of 11 matches unbeaten, advancing to the Premier Sports Cup final with victory over Aberdeen at Hampden this weekend.

But McInnes hasn't forgotten the early struggles as he joked with Jeff Stelling and McCoist on talkSPORT on Monday.

In a quip in response to Stelling's introduction discussing the challenges in the early stages of the season, McInnes said: "You've underestimated that slightly rocky part I think!"

The live stream then cut to McCoist who was doubled over at McInnes' honest assessment.

McInnes continued: "When you get a new job, it's normally for a reason – nothing is normally perfect. We had lots of work to do, but underneath it all, I felt if we came out the window with a strong enough squad, then we could compete. That's where we are at the minute.

"We needed a bit of confidence. The run started up at Aberdeen, going 11 games [unbeaten], and we're pleased with what we're doing. There's still a lot of improvement [needed]. But as Ally knows, at Rangers, we need to keep winning.

"The noise and everything that comes with it when you're not winning makes things so much more difficult.

"But I'm delighted with the response of the players. The game on Saturday was another case in point. We were the better team, we created more chances, we look as if we're scoring, but it took us too long to get the winning goal. But when it came, it was a great moment for us, and we look forward to the final now."

On there being progress to be made by his Rangers side, McInnes added: "There has to be (more improvement to come). No team is perfect at this stage of the season, the season is still in its infancy.

"People are so quick to judge and assume this is how it's going to be, but it's so early on. There's loads of improvements to come from us, but that's the same with most teams.

"We're a very young team, particularly in the forward line.

"A lot of stats will back that up. Sometimes we could do with a bit more nous and an older head up there just to try and make better decisions. But the potential is exciting, and the reach of some of these players is evident. But we need to try and win as we search for that potential."

#2079. This is where the match was lost as it ends Newcastle 0 Everton 1

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Newcastle 0 Everton 1 – Monday 2 November 2026 8pm

Everton seemed to have at least one extra player nearly all evening.

They used the ball better and with accurate finishing would have scored twice before half-time.

Newcastle, perhaps nervous of throwing men forward after being exposed last Thursday, rarely threatened. Our midfield and defence still looked scarily open, however.

Hall and Dedic were apparently being expected to play simultaneously in defence and attack, with predictable results when possession was turned over.

The first save either keeper had to make fell to Lukas Hornicek just after the interval. He let a routine shot slide under his body. Barry couldn’t miss and the officials did the rest, deciding a dubious challenge on Schar in the build-up was legal.

Hornicek prevented Dewsbury-Hall from doubling the lead, then did well to block a Branthwaite header.

On 64 minutes, Steur and Wissa replaced Gonzalez and Willock. Within two minutes we nearly levelled but Elanga’s point-blank shot rolled along the line before being cleared.

As the game became spread, Schar stopped a second Barry tap-in with a great but risky challenge. Murphy and Ramsey replaced Elanga and Joelinton with 15 minutes left. Ramsey was a yard wide from hitting the jackpot on 79 minutes but still Pickford had not been extended.

The save he made from a weak 20-yarder by Wissa was as easy as Everton made their victory look. Conversely, United struggled to do much right.

Pickford finally earned his wage by kicking clear a Wissa snap shot after good work down the left by Toure, the last sub.

Deep into stoppage time, Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession, the second for an ugly tackle.

The bumps on the road are becoming bigger and more frequent.

#2076. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2073. Nuno’s West Ham Future Under Threat As Board Concerns Grow

Nuno Espírito Santo’s position as West Ham United manager is under increasing threat, according to a new report from The Guardian. With the Hammers slipping to eighth in the Championship following consecutive home defeats, patience is reportedly wearing thin among key figures at the London Stadium.

Writing for The Guardian, Hammers fan Jacob Steinberg reports that although Nuno is expected to be given more time to turn things around, influential figures at West Ham are becoming increasingly impatient with the club’s disappointing start to the season.

The report comes just two days after the 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, a result which prompted further questions about Nuno’s tactics and his ability to get the best out of a squad assembled with the intention of securing an immediate return to the Premier League.

According to The Guardian, any decision regarding Nuno’s future would be taken collectively by the West Ham board, rather than by one shareholder acting alone.

Interim chief executive Karim Virani and recruitment director Nils Koppen are among those expected to have input.

The report also revisits the decision to retain Nuno following relegation, explaining that David Sullivan had wanted a change of manager while Daniel Křetínský favoured continuity.

However, that previous support does not necessarily mean the manager’s position is secure indefinitely.

West Ham have won just twice in their last six Championship matches, and the upcoming fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers could become increasingly important ahead of the November international break.

The Guardian also highlights concerns about Nuno’s inability to settle on his strongest starting eleven, the lack of balance in midfield and the failure of the club’s strikers to provide sufficient goals.

The report states that West Ham’s three recognised centre-forwards, Joël Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos, have scored just five league goals between them this season.

Meanwhile, Jarrod Bowen has scored seven, leaving the Hammers heavily dependent on our captain.

The continued absence of recognised defensive midfielders Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez from Nuno’s preferred selections is another issue raised.

These concerns will sound familiar to Claret & Hugh readers. Following the West Brom defeat, I questioned whether Nuno’s entire West Ham project was becoming fundamentally flawed, particularly given the lack of cohesion and the manager’s constant tactical changes.

And while I appreciate that managers need time, I struggle to see how West Ham can continue performing so poorly with a squad that should be capable of competing for automatic promotion.

Perhaps the most important aspect of The Guardian’s report is the suggestion that Nuno will face difficult questions if performances fail to improve before the international break.

There is no suggestion that a dismissal has already been agreed, and the report specifically indicates that West Ham still hope the manager can turn things around.

Nevertheless, it appears the pressure is no longer coming exclusively from frustrated supporters.

The next two matches now offer Nuno an opportunity to demonstrate that he can produce a convincing response.

Because as I’ve argued previously, West Ham’s problems haven’t suddenly appeared over the last fortnight. The warning signs have been there for considerably longer.

And if the manager cannot begin addressing them, it is becoming increasingly difficult to see how the club can justify continuing with the same approach.

#2072. Ally McCoist reveals vital Rangers transfer advice for star man Olwethu Makhanya

Ally McCoist reckons Olwethu Makhanya should have no thoughts of leaving Rangers any time soon despite attracting attention with his outstanding start to life at Ibrox.

The South African defender has emerged as one of the club's standout performers since arriving from Philadelphia Union in a £3million deal. Comfortable at centre-back and capable of covering on the left side of defence, Makhanya has become a key figure in Derek McInnes' plans.

His impressive form has inevitably sparked talk of interest from elsewhere, but Rangers legend McCoist believes the 22-year-old is in the ideal place to continue his development and establish himself further.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, McCoist said: "Pat Nevin generally talks an awful lot of sense, and he's spot on here. I don't think Makhanya should be in any rush to go anywhere.

Read more: Thelo Aasgaard receives glowing 'DNA' praise on Rangers loan exit

"He's had a very good start, though the weekend was maybe a little reminder that you don't get any easy games and you're a target.

"So, from that point of view, there's no doubt that with the way he's started, there will be clubs looking at him.

"But I would be advising him to stay for a while, get the job done, keep getting rave reports, and see where it takes him."

McCoist is also encouraged by the progress Rangers have made under McInnes and insists the club's ambitions should remain as high as ever despite their European disappointment.

The former striker believes domestic success must be the priority, with the Premiership title remaining the ultimate target.

He added: "I don't think anything has changed. I think Rangers have got to set out right now to win every domestic trophy they can.

"You have to be looking to win the league title, that is the most important one at the start of the season for a team like Rangers.

"The Cups I always say are a more than achievable bonus, but you've got to get the league title.

"That is still the priority for me looking at it, and the priority for most Rangers fans right now."

#2069. Cardiff City v West Ham: Lineups And Predicted Teams For Huge Championship Clash

Cardiff City v West Ham United EFL Championship Cardiff City Stadium Wednesday 4 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

West Ham United’s trip to Cardiff City is hugely important. Lose this one and I believe Nuno Espírito Santo will have a very real chance of losing his job following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion.

Saturday’s 3-1 loss has already dropped the Hammers to eighth, occupying the final play-off position. Another defeat could see us unceremoniously dumped out of the top eight and further towards mid-table, which would be an extraordinary situation for a club widely expected to challenge for automatic promotion.

This is therefore about far more than collecting three points against a newly promoted team. Nuno needs a result to arrest West Ham’s decline, restore some belief among the players and demonstrate that he remains capable of rescuing a promotion campaign which is beginning to unravel.

The most concerning part of the 3-1 defeat against West Brom was the players’ apparent lack of motivation and the absence of any recognisable tactical plan.

West Ham do not seem capable of defending or attacking properly at the moment. The defence is repeatedly exposed by simple passages of play, while the attack remains heavily dependent on Jarrod Bowen producing something individually.

Nuno admitted afterwards that it was a poor performance and that West Ham conceded too easily. However, the same weaknesses have been visible for some time, and words will mean very little unless something changes on the pitch.

The team lacks cohesion, urgency and confidence. More worryingly, there is increasingly little evidence that the players understand precisely what the manager wants them to do.

Reports have already questioned whether West Ham’s players are still fighting for Nuno. Wednesday night should provide a fairly clear answer.

Nuno Espírito Santo needs to pull himself and his team together ahead of Wednesday

I believe Nuno is capable of turning this around in the immediate sense. West Ham have enough individual quality to beat Cardiff and Blackburn, even while playing considerably below the level expected of this squad.

What I am far less convinced about is whether he possesses the necessary man-management and tactical skills to turn West Ham into a team comfortably established inside the automatic promotion places.

Those are two different questions. Winning the next two matches may ease the pressure, but it would not automatically prove that Nuno has solved the underlying problems which have followed West Ham throughout the season.

I have already explained why I believe Nuno has had long enough and West Ham need a change. Nothing about the West Brom performance altered that conclusion.

My preferred formation would be a 4-1-4-1, accompanied by drastic changes in personnel.

Alphonse Areola would replace Mads Hermansen in goal. Nobody should be guaranteed a place during such a poor run, and Hermansen has not done enough to make himself untouchable.

Joël Veltman would start at right-back, with Airidas Golambeckis partnering Max Kilman in central defence if Konstantinos Mavropanos remains unavailable. Kyle Walker-Peters would move to left-back, assuming he recovers from the injury sustained against West Brom.

Soungoutou Magassa would operate as the holding midfielder. West Ham desperately need somebody to protect the defence, and the repeated decision to play without a natural defensive midfielder has contributed to the team’s lack of balance.

Lewis Orford and Divine Mukasa would play ahead of him, giving West Ham energy, creativity and players capable of retaining possession. Bowen and Edvin Austbø would provide the width, with Joël Piroe given a proper opportunity as the central striker.

These are broadly the immediate changes I believe Nuno needs to make. Repeating the same selections and expecting a different performance no longer makes any sense.

This is the team I would select at Cardiff, built around a recognised holding midfielder and players who deserve an opportunity. Walker-Peters is a fitness doubt, so his inclusion depends on him recovering in time.

Managers under pressure rarely make radical changes, which is why I expect Nuno’s selection to look rather different from mine.

I still believe he could replace Hermansen with Areola and retain Veltman at right-back. Golambeckis should continue alongside Kilman if Mavropanos remains unavailable, but I expect Morato to keep his place at left-back.

Mohamadou Kanté and Arne Engels are likely to form the central-midfield partnership, with Manor Solomon operating behind Piroe. Bowen and Austbø should provide the width in what looks like a 4-2-3-1.

Cardiff sit 17th after gaining promotion as League One runners-up last season. Their recent unbeaten run ended with a 3-0 defeat at Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday.

The Bluebirds have significant problems in defence. Gabriel Osho is suspended, while Dylan Lawlor and Calum Chambers have been sidelined through injury.

Manager Brian Barry-Murphy also revealed fresh concerns following the Wolves defeat, with Will Fish suffering a hamstring problem, Perry Ng struggling with fitness and Alex Robertson experiencing an Achilles issue. Krystian Bielik remains another doubt, although he has returned to training.

That leaves Cardiff facing the possibility of several important absences, although not every player mentioned has been ruled out of Wednesday’s match.

West Ham have their own concerns, with Mavropanos recovering from a knee problem and Walker-Peters doubtful following his injury against West Brom.

However, Nuno cannot reasonably claim he has been handed an impossible assignment.

Cardiff’s problems give West Ham an opportunity to stop the rot. If the Hammers cannot produce a convincing response against a newly promoted side with such significant defensive concerns, the pressure surrounding Nuno’s position will become increasingly difficult to ignore.

On paper, West Ham should win this match. We possess the stronger and more expensive squad, while Cardiff could be without a significant number of players.

Unfortunately, nothing about West Ham’s recent performances inspires confidence. The players look short of motivation, the defence is vulnerable and there is no obvious attacking plan beyond hoping Bowen creates something.

I believe Nuno is capable of winning the next two games, but I cannot predict it with any confidence. My expectation is that West Ham will stop the run of defeats without doing enough to claim the victory they desperately need.

Prediction: Cardiff City 1-1 West Ham United

#2068. ‘Really poor’ – Steven Gerrard left raging over ‘absolute embarrassment’ at Anfield on Sunday

Steven Gerrard described the failure of Stuart Attwell on VAR to intervene over a crucial decision at Anfield on Sunday as ‘an absolute embarrassment’.

There was controversy in the 21st minute of Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak’s shirt inside the penalty area, a clear foul which somehow went unpunished just five minutes after Kai Havertz’s winning goal.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola went as far as to suggest that he’d encourage his players to go to ground in such situations, with the Swedish striker staying on his feet and not protesting to the referee despite the obvious offence on him.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard was aghast at how Attwell on VAR failed to intervene over the incident involving Timber and Isak.

The ex-Liverpool captain said: “The speed of the cross and how it happened and the reaction, you can understand how a referee could possibly miss that or think there’s not much in that, but for someone to sit in [the VAR room] with all these screens around – how you miss that in the VAR seat is an absolute embarrassment.”

He added: “To hold someone’s shirt for that long and have three or four opportunities to see that and slow it down, and the amount of cameras that are in stadia at the moment, it’s really poor from Stuart Attwell.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Gerrard’s incredulity over the lack of intervention from Attwell is quite justified – the official on VAR majorly dropped the ball in that instance.

We can absolve on-field referee Andy Madley to an extent, although the shirt tug was so blatant that he could viably have spotted it too, but there’s no excuse whatsoever for those in Stockley Park to let it slide.

VAR was brought in with the intetention of correcting ‘clear and obvious’ errors, and what Timber did to Isak yesterday very much meets that description. Why, then, did Attwell not recommend a pitchside review to the ref when it would’ve been very much warranted?

Some decisions are quite subjective even when slowed down or viewed from multiple angles, but this seemed like one of the more clear-cut calls to make, yet nobody with the power to take action was proactive enough to do so.

In a tight game settled by that early goal from Havertz, it had a significant impact on the final outcome, and Liverpool have every right to be apoplectic at bearing the brunt of that baffling call by the officials.

#2067. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#2065. Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

Rangers manager Derek McInnes has stated Falkirk's win over Celtic was "not really a shock".

The Ibrox boss commented on the weekend result when he appeared on talkSPORT on Monday morning, as he hailed the work done by John McGlynn.

Ally McCoist had singled out McGlynn for praise for the job he has done at Falkirk - and McInnes joined in on heaping praise on the manager.

And he insisted it wasn't a huge shock to see Falkirk beat Celtic.

"Although it seems a shock Celtic getting beat there, but it's not really a shock when you see it's Falkirk that win the game.

"Falkirk are capable of that, and they did that a couple of times last season as well."

McInnes then backed his former club Hearts to be in the title hunt this season.

He said: "I do think Hearts will be title contenders again with the investment and size of squad they have got and the level of player they have got.

"I think Hearts will be up there again. It will be more of a surprise if they're not."

#2064. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#2063. Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

Rangers icon Ally McCoist has revealed he would hate to see Celtic boss Martin O'Neill suffer and reckons the veteran manager has earned the right to walk away on his own terms.

The Ibrox hero, who has long admired O'Neill despite their rivalry, admits his biggest concern is the toll management can take on the 74-year-old's health. While McCoist hopes close friend Derek McInnes can guide Rangers to title glory this season, he stressed he would take no pleasure in seeing O'Neill pushed out of Parkhead or forced to continue beyond the point where the job remains enjoyable.

The former Rangers striker believes O'Neill's decades of service to the game, and his achievements at Celtic, mean he deserves the respect to decide for himself when the time is right to step aside.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, the 64-year-old said: "I think Martin has absolutely earned the right and deserves the respect to stay for as long as he feels right. I really do.

"I would hate Martin to overstay his time at Celtic, first and foremost for his health.

Read more: Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

"That's the most important thing, because I've always gotten on really well with Martin. Obviously I want Rangers to win the league 100 per cent, but Martin has more than earned the right to see things out for as long as he wants at Celtic, and that should be the case."

McCoist also concedes Europe's demands could yet play a significant role in the title race.

"I don't think for a minute Martin will say they're prioritising, but their level of performance in Europe has been extremely disappointing. I know they created one or two chances against Benfica, but Benfica were three-nil up and done.

"The performances in Europe have been really disappointing from Martin's point of view.

"I don't have any doubt that it could work in Rangers' favour not having those Thursday European games. Celtic are not allowed, same as Rangers, to get into any game other than expecting to win, particularly at home, whether domestic or European, the fans won't allow it.

"So there is added pressure on Celtic, of course there is. But Martin will be delighted with their league form. I noticed a lovely quote from him this morning where he said it was a fantastic result at the weekend, but if they get beaten on Thursday there'll be another crisis!

#2062. “One of the best nights of my life” – Bologna duo react after comeback win vs. Milan

Samuel Mbangula labelled scoring a hat-trick against AC Milan as ‘one of the best nights’ of his life, as he fired Bologna to victory.

It was a rollercoaster night at San Siro, one in which Milan trailed early on, then came back to lead, before a complete collapse in the second half that left sections of the fans jeering as the final few minutes played out.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan trailed early to a goal from Samuel Mbangula, but they went into half-time 2-1 up thanks to Alphadjo Cisse’s brace. The second half was a disaster though as an own-goal and two more from Mbangula allowed Bologna to inflict a first league defeat of the season on the Rossoneri.

Mbangula spoke to DAZN after the full-time whistle to give his thoughts on what was a very memorable evening for him, as he opened his account for his new club after the summer move.

“It’s one of the best nights of my life. First hat-trick of my career, I hope it’s not the last. It was a beautiful victory. The coach has great confidence, everyone is strong and can play. We are united, today is a team victory,” he said (via MilanNews).

Alongside the match-winner, Bologna goalkeeper Lukasz Skorupski spoke to DAZN about the victory as well, praising the strength of the team’s reaction.

“Perhaps the best thing was the team’s reaction. We were down 2-1, but in the end we won 4-2. We’ll enjoy it tonight, then we’ll immediately think about Saturday, where we have another match. Mbangula’s hat-trick? I told him he has to take us out to dinner next week.”

#2059. Rangers star called up by under-21 national team after being dropped from full squad

Rangers star Kim Min-su has been named in South Korea's under-21 squad instead, after he was dropped from their full squad.

The Ibrox ace made his international debut for his country last month and played in three friendlies against Ecuador, Uruguay and Venezuela and was an unused sub against Uzbekistan.

But that wasn't enough to see him included in South Korea's latest squad for their games against Qatar and Saudi Arabia later this month.

However, he has now been included in their under-21s squad for two friendlies against Mexico.

The squad doubles as South Korea's Olympic team for the football section of the Games in two years' time in Los Angeles.

South Korea Under 21s boss Kim Eun-joong said: "This is a good opportunity to gain practical experience against a strong team, Mexico.

"We will identify areas for improvement and take our competitiveness up a level."

Kim will travel to his homeland for the two games against the Mexicans at Cheonan on November 14 and a rematch against the same opponents three days later at the same venue.

#2058. Five get below half-marks: Fan player ratings for Milan 2-4 Bologna

AC Milan’s unbeaten record in Serie A fell on Thursday night after a disastrous second-half performance against Bologna.

Milan started the game badly on the night with Samuel Mbangula putting Bologna 1-0 up, but Alphadjo Cisse scored twice in relatively quick succession – his first two goals at home – to put the Rossoneri in front going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, the second half was a total catastrophe. An own-goal drew Raffaele Palladino’s side level, then two minutes later they led again with Mbangula scoring, and the Belgian got his hat-trick late on to secure a quite remarkable 4-2 win.

We published our ratings on the final whistle, and now we can compare them with what our readers thought of the performances of each player involved.

Going on the presumption that a 6 out of 10 is a passing grade (as the Italian papers do it), there were only four players in the starting line-up that managed to achieve that. Fikayo Tomori scored a 6.1 on average, while Ardon Jashari got the same, Omari Hutchinson was awarded a 6.4 and Cisse a 7.3.

The stand-out scores in a negative sense are Pervis Estupinan (2.9) and Goncalo Ramos (3.8). Koni De Winter, Yunus Musah (both 4.5s) and Davide Bartesaghi (4.9) all didn’t even get half marks.

The substitutes were a mixed bag too, with Sankhoun Diawara’ 4.6 and Francesco Camarda’s 4.8 the worst, but even Luka Modric and Christian Pulisic (5.6s) didn’t get a pass this time.
