#2031. Moreira lifts lid on Kaka-inspired number choice, first derby and friendship with Rabiot

Diego Moreira is gearing up for his first derby as an AC Milan player, and he is very much relishing the occasion.

Moreira was the second big splash in the summer window for Milan, after the club-record signing of Goncalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain. The Belgian has already impressed with three goals to his name, including a brace that rescued a draw against Lazio in the capital.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having sat out of the last two games against Udinese and Bologna, the good news is that Moreira has recovered from his muscle issue and will therefore be available to the head coach Ruben Amorim for tomorrow night’s derby.

He spoke to DAZN in the ‘Remember The Name’ programme in an interview that was broadcast on the eve of the game, with his words relayed by MilanVibes.

“My name is Diego because it was my mother’s favourite name. She adored Diego Maradona and really liked it. When people analyse it, they say that with this name I seem to be made to play football, so I really like it.

“My Instagram name? My godfather’s name is Armizy on social media, and I copied it. I spend a lot of time with him. When I was little, I used to play football everywhere and break everything.

“My dream was to become a professional footballer, and we’re almost there, come on (laughs). I left home at 15, a very difficult time for my mother, but now we’re happy because I’ve achieved my dream of becoming a footballer, and the sacrifices we made have led to this.

“My mom is very important to me, she’s unique, and everything we’ve been through now makes us happy. I talk to dad often, and when I finish games and they don’t go well, I only talk to him because I know we’ll talk about football and nothing else.

“He was the one who called me and told me about AC Milan’s interest, he was just waiting for me to say yes or no. When AC Milan calls you, you can’t say no. My tattoos speak of my family, even my grandparents.”

You have spoken before about Hazard, Kaka and Cristiano Ronaldo…

“Eden is a gem. A champion, an inspiration: when you grow up watching him, you try his moves and hope to be able to do them on the pitch one day. Cristiano is my idol, a champion, the greatest.

“As a kid, I wanted to be him, to have my hair cut like him, but I had too much. He made me believe in myself and pushed me to play football. I’m happy to have enjoyed his prime.

“Kaka? I wanted number 7. When they told me it was available, I was tempted to take it, but I like number 22. I hope to honour it and do well enough to deserve this number.”

“Milan-Inter is one of the biggest derbies in Europe. We’re fired up, I’d die for my team and to play these games, we’re fired up.”

You have struck up a friendship with Rabiot…

“From the first few days, Adrien has been one of the ones who welcomed me best, especially because he speaks French.

“We talk a lot, especially because we’re always the last ones in the dressing room, so we often eat together and talk about life, football, everything. I also really enjoy being on the pitch, so that helps us get along.”

“The fact that I have a strong personality has helped me settle in. I feel great in this group and they understand me. We have to win games to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be: we have quality, spirit, a great group and we have to do it.”

#2026. Hibs' astonishing 47-year Hampden record vs Rangers sets up classic

Hibernian head into next month's Premier Sports Cup Final against Rangers with their tails up.

Granted the club's Scottish Premiership form leaves plenty to be desired, but their semi-final victory over fierce rivals Hearts on Sunday afternoon highlighted the fighting spirit still within the camp.

Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath's goals cancelled out Claudio Braga's early opener and set up the showpiece finale at Hampden Park on December 13. And it turns out Hibs have more to be excited and confident about given their history against the Light Blues at the national stadium.

Marink Reedijk's squad will square off against Derek McInnes' charges and they will do so with the bit between their teeth in the competition. But they also have history on their side.

Hibs have astonishingly not been beaten by Rangers at Hampden in a whopping 47 years.

The last time the Glasgow outfit came out on top was at the 1979 Scottish Cup final which took three attempts following a goalless draw in the initial final and then another in the replay. Rangers would win the third contest 3-2.

Since that period the two clubs have faced off four more times at Hampden and the Leith side have come out on top each time.

First came in the League Cup semi-final of 1991 when Keith Wright netted the winner inside the first 30 minutes. Then in 2004 Hibs progressed to the final of the same competition with a penalty shootout victory over their opponents following a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Stephen Dobbie had levelled after Michael Mols had opened the scoring for Gers during normal time.

The iconic 2016 Scottish Cup Final was next when former defender and then head coach David Gray bulleted home the winning header after an exhausting 3-2 victory for Hibs.

And in 2021 Hibs continued their reign of Hampden dominance over Rangers when they knocked them out of the League Cup at the semi-final stage again. Boyle fired in a stunning first-half hattrick before Scott Arfield nicked a consolation.

It's a staggering statistic and one Hibs will be desperate to add to when the final rolls around next month.

#2022. Musah talks second chance at Milan, upcoming derby, Modric and other team-mates

The media coverage has ramped up into overdrive on the eve of the derby, with Yunus Musah the latest to speak ahead of the game.

Musah spent last season out on loan at Atalanta with Massimiliano Allegri not deeming him to be a part of his plans, but he returned in the summer as the Bergamo club did not use the option to buy. Many thought he would be packing his suitcases again, but that wasn’t the case.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Instead, the new head coach Ruben Amorim has placed a great deal of faith in the American, using him in a deeper midfield role which seems to be bringing out the best from him. He has previously spoken about feeling ‘grateful’ to have been given a fresh chance by Amorim.

Musah spoke in an interview with CBS Sports to preview Saturday night’s big game, one in which Milan really need three points in order to reduce the gap to the top of the standings. His words are via MilanNews.

“There’s still a long way to go, but after losing a season, I’ve learned that even in crucial moments, you have to keep going. Now I’m really keen to stay. I want to stay at this club and do really well here. The coach is helping me a lot, giving me opportunities that I need to seize.”

Considering what you went through last year, you’ve become the most used central midfielder this season: what instructions did the coach give you? What was the first thing he said to you when you spoke?

“Nothing complicated. The coaching staff works as a team, so the entire team knows exactly what each member is doing. They give us all the necessary instructions: how to receive the ball, how to read the various moments of the game, and how to interpret the play according to their instructions.

“This allows me to step onto the pitch without any hesitation. It’s a huge help, because when you step onto the pitch, you know exactly what you have to do.”

Can you better understand where you might not be recognised?

“For example, sometimes at the supermarket, when there aren’t many people, someone still stares at me, everyone wants to say hello or ask me something because everyone knows and watches AC Milan.

“Then, at a club where winning every single match is crucial, other teams approach AC Milan differently: for them, it’s the most important match of the season. Every match is difficult, everything has changed. Sometimes, to escape this celebrity aura, I go shopping at the supermarket at night.”

Knowing that Luka Modrić has been my favourite player for about 10-15 years, and given that you have the opportunity to train with him every day, what’s it like being around him?

“Yes, I try to enjoy the moment and the time I can spend with him. It won’t be many years, so I really appreciate every moment we spend together in midfield. In the past, when he played for Real Madrid, I managed to get a shirt.

“The world of football is really small, but now we find ourselves playing together, side by side in midfield. It’s unreal. It’s fantastic to share the dressing room with him, to be on the pitch with him.

“I’m learning so many things on the pitch just by watching him. Sometimes we speak Spanish, he speaks both English and Spanish well.”

“It’s a different game than the others. When you train for the derby, it’s more special. You don’t have to tell any of your teammates how important the game is or that they need to focus on it.

“Everyone is focused, working hard because it’s incredibly important for our fans, for us. It’s the game where, when you win, it’s like you’ve won a trophy. I’m very focused on this match.”

How difficult is it to focus on the games before the derby knowing that the match is so close?

“I think before the match, we all know the derby is close, but we’re focusing on the games we have to play first, then when the match comes, we’ll think about it. Clearly, it’s very important to win and take home the three points.”

Who did you grow up with as an AC Milan or Italian football idol? Who did you watch as a child?

“I really liked Ronaldinho, but I didn’t watch much football back then. I watched him more later, even through highlights. When I was little, I played football a lot more than I watched it. I enjoyed playing. Every day I’d go out with my brother and my friends and we’d spend hours playing.

“I love those days, out in the street playing. Anyway, Ronaldinho was a great player, and that’s why I chose the number 80 when I arrived at Milan.”

Who is most likely to become a coach after a playing career?

“Matteo Gabbia is truly tactically savvy.”

Who is most likely to become a social media influencer?

“I would have said Rafa but now I say Diego Moreira.”

Who is most likely to lose one of the three essential items: phone, wallet, or keys?

“Mario Gila always loses a lot of things, like on airplanes. Yes, definitely him. He needs those Apple gadgets, what are they called? AirTags! Yes, we need to give him some AirTags for Christmas.”

And who could survive the longest on a desert island?

“I’d say, I like it! I’m very resourceful, you know?

What’s the secret to surviving on a desert island? You seem very confident…

“I wouldn’t let the pressure get me down. I’d work hard, I’d try to find everything I needed to survive, I’d go fishing.”

The team most likely to win the Milan derby is?

#2018. GdS: Milan vs. Inter to be a ‘full’ sell-out for the first time since 2019 – the reason

The derby between AC Milan and Inter on Saturday night will be a full sell-out for the first time in over half a decade.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, it is as if there has been a surge in pride just hours after the unveiling of the new stadium that will replace it in five years. San Siro opens its arms even wider for tomorrow’s derby, as it has for over 100 years.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The highest possible capacity can be sold: for the occasion, the safety curtains located in the two stands will be removed, namely, the Terzo Anello Blu (South) and Terzo Anello Verde (North). This means that San Siro will be a sellout in the truest sense of the word.

The last time it happened was for the derby on 17 March 2019, with 77,479 spectators. A total of 2,350 additional seats are available: this is the amount that was removed from the stadium’s capacity in the summer of 2019, which became effective starting with the 2019-20 football season.

The decision was made by the Provincial Supervisory Commission and implemented by the City of Milan and the MI Stadio, following observations by the technical commission, which also included the Polytechnic University, of the vibrations felt particularly in those areas (sectors 349-351-352 of the Green third and 307-309-310 of the Blue third).

This measure, however, was not related to a true safety issue, but was considered ‘managerial’ by the technicians at Palazzo Marino: the aim was to prevent fear from spreading among fans when they felt the vibrations.

It’s worth noting that the absence of restrictions will apply to both the league and the Coppa Italia: in the Europa League for AC Milan and the Champions League for Inter, the screens will be regularly placed in the centre of the away stands.

Anyone entering San Siro, however, has been accustomed for years to seeing those three blue and green rectangles located in the stands at the centre of the third tier. Now they will no longer be there: San Siro is destined to say goodbye, but for now it’s only revving up.

#2017. Police launch investigation after officers targeted before Aberdeen-Rangers match

An investigation into “unacceptable” football-related disorder where officers were targeted with fireworks and glass bottles has been launched by police.

On Monday, Police Scotland said it is looking into the matter, which took place on Curtis Avenue, Glasgow, ahead of the Aberdeen versus Rangers game that kicked off at 5.30pm on Saturday.

Police said officers had glass bottles, fireworks and other projectiles launched at them, with two fans being assaulted, though they did not need medical attention.

A man was arrested in a separate incident outside Hampden in connection with an assault, but there were no arrests made during the match.

The following day, at Hearts versus Hibernian at Hampden, four men, aged between 24 and 37, were arrested for possession of pyrotechnics and abusive behaviour, and are due at Glasgow Sheriff Court at a later date.

Teenage taken to hospital after serious assault near Glasgow Central

Child in pram injured after firework thrown at woman and children in Glasgow

The riot we knew was coming to Scotland. We have to stop it happening again

Officer jailed for rape and sexual assault launches bid to overturn conviction

Another man was charged for alleged vandalism and two other men received police warnings for threatening and abusive behaviour.

A 28-year-old man was later arrested and charged outside the stadium for similar offences, and one more man was given a warning for the same.

An additional three men and one woman are also to be reported to the Procurator Fiscal for the same, as well as pyrotechnic offences.

Superintendent Paul Douglas said: “Several officers were assaulted whilst carrying out their duties during unacceptable disorder ahead of the Aberdeen v Rangers match at Hampden on Saturday October 31 2026.

“They were attacked with fireworks, glass bottles and other missiles as supporters gathered in the Curtis Street area of Glasgow before kick-off.

“This violence is disgraceful and will not be tolerated. Being assaulted is not part of the job and it’s extremely fortunate they were not seriously injured.

“Two fans were also assaulted during the same incident but did not require hospital treatment.

“Those involved should be in no doubt that they will be identified and arrested. Inquiries are ongoing to trace those responsible and we will work closely with both football clubs as part of our investigation.

“I would appeal to the public for information and urge anyone who knows who was involved in this disorder to contact Police Scotland via 101, quoting incident 1676 of October 31.

“We recognise that only a small percentage of fans behave in such a way and cause disorder, but I would encourage all fans to take personal responsibility for their conduct.”

#2016. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#2015. Sunday's La Liga predictions including Racing Santander vs. Real Madrid, Athletic Bilbao vs. Real Sociedad

By Ben Sully | 01 Nov 2026 00:10, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 00:10

Today's La Liga predictions include Real Madrid's away clash against Racing de Santander and the must-watch Basque derby between Athletic Bilbao and Real Sociedad.

Sevilla will aim to make it three straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign away to Getafe on Sunday afternoon.

The visitors are currently sixth in the La Liga table, boasting 17 points from their opening 10 matches of the campaign, while Getafe are 17th in the division on nine points.

Sevilla have won their last two matches, and we are backing the visitors to secure another victory here against a Getafe team that are struggling in the final third of the field.

Real Madrid will be aiming to make it six straight wins in all competitions when they tackle Racing de Santander at El Sardinero on Sunday afternoon.

#2014. Amorim discusses Cardinale’s ‘Top Gun’ remark, Scudetto aim, Ramos’ struggles and injuries

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has responded to Gerry Cardinale’s words about him being his ‘Top Gun’ and the Scudetto being an aim.

For Milan, there is once again the need to bounce back after a negative result. On Wednesday night at San Siro they led at half-time against Bologna, before conceding three times in the second half to eventually lose 4-2.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Not only did that knock the Rossoneri out of the top four but it put them seven points behind Inter and Lazio who are the league-leaders at the moment. So, it means that a victory is needed in the derby to keep pace at the top, but there is at least some good injury news: Diego Moreira, Mario Gila and Adrien Rabiot are all back.

Amorim spoke to the reporters who gathered at Milanello for his pre-match press conference on the eve of the game. MilanNews relayed his words.

“I truly appreciate Cardinale’s support. We already knew – and everyone here has the clarity to understand – that we can’t build a solid foundation if we have to deal with these kinds of issues in the middle of the season.

“It will take time, it’s inevitable, but at the same time, we want to win every single game: when we fail to do so, we’ll continue to feel it, making it our own with great pain. It will be like this for a while. We need time to grow and improve the team, and we know that good things take time to find the perfect balance and hit the mark.

“I think it’s a good analogy and it makes perfect sense, but that doesn’t take away the pain of defeat. That’s still there, it still stings, but we need to be extremely clear with our fans, making them understand that it will take time.”

What differences do you feel between this derby and the ones in Manchester and Lisbon?

“I think it’s a special match because it’s being played in the same city, and yesterday we saw the plans for the new stadium. It’s a unique rivalry, but there’s also a deep bond: two great teams in the same city sharing a stadium.

“I don’t think you can find a context like this anywhere else; it’s truly special. But matches like this… well, if we look at Portuguese culture, the feeling is the same: the sense of responsibility for victory, the enthusiasm of the fans, are very similar. The football culture here is closer to that of Portugal.

“In England, it’s slightly different: there’s a great battle, but the spirit remains a bit more sporting. Here, you can feel that Latin element that we also experience in Portugal, so I really think it will be a special match.”

“They’re ready to join the team. We’ll have to evaluate tomorrow morning whether they’ll be able to start or what the game plan will be. Of course, I already have an idea, but we’ll see tomorrow.”

Has the team regained the energy it didn’t see on Wednesday?

“Everyone knows it’s a special match, a special moment, and when you get to play it, the context doesn’t matter, it doesn’t matter if you’re tired. You have to go out there and give it your all, and we’ll be there.

“I said it: I felt it from the first minute of the match against Bologna, watching the game from the bench. We can’t lose a game like that. We can’t afford to concede two goals in two minutes. We can do much better, and there are so many small details that I’ve already discussed with the team.

“But since we returned from international duty three weeks ago, there hasn’t been any real time to train. And I’m not saying other teams are in a different position, I’m speaking for ourselves: I feel like there are so many small things we’re missing simply because we don’t have the time to address them in training.

“So it’s not just a question of energy, although I’ve noticed that, because with energy you can also mask a lot of shortcomings, but there are so many aspects we need time to work on if we want to become a better team.”

Cardinale says that the Scudetto is possible this year and that there will be some signings in January…

“You always have to talk about the Scudetto as the main objective when you’re at Milan, but we’ve already dropped points and we need to fix things. We just have to focus on improving the team step by step.

“What we did wrong in the last match needs to be corrected for the next one. Because if we start thinking too far ahead, about the standings and long-term goals, we risk forgetting what’s really important to us. We want to win consistently, year after year.

“We don’t want to win a season just because we had a bit of luck or because we took shortcuts in the foundations of the project, only to find ourselves back where we started the following year. That’s why we have to fix things day by day, addressing both needs in parallel.

“But when you’re Milan, the moral obligation is to declare that the objective is to win. And at the same time, we have to be aware that next week we have a match that could allow us to close the gap at the top.

“Taking all this into account, we just have to focus on winning the next match, and everything else will calm down. But the objective of the club is always and in any case winning Serie A and that remains our final goal. How long will it take? I don’t know.”

“I have zero envy for Chivu because I’m already in the right place, that is, at Milan and not at Inter. That’s the way I am, that’s the way I am.

“I haven’t learned the lesson from my previous experience: I chose more or less the same situation, a club in the midst of rebuilding, which is trying to launch young players like Cisse to build something from scratch.

“It’s a challenge that excites me, I like it, and that’s why I chose this project: I’m really happy with my choice. At the same time, however, I’m not naive: I know very well that you have to win games to buy yourself the time necessary to build something lasting.

“Everyone chooses their own path, and this is mine. Whether it will work or not, no one can know anything now, but I’m really happy because this reflects exactly who I am and the type of work I want to do.

“I understand the questions you ask me: there are days when, in the morning, I think that perhaps I could have had more experience, more calm, a larger squad, fewer injuries. But at the end of the day, I was the one who chose this job, so I’m very happy with it and I’ll go all the way, straight down my path.

“You already know: if I embrace an idea, I certainly don’t change my mind. I can change the tactical system, sure, but I won’t change my conviction, and I’ll do everything I can to win and be successful here.”

What do you think of Inter? Did you speak to Chivu yesterday?

“He’s very nice. We were complaining a bit about the timing of the presentation because we’d played the night before: he won, so he was happier than me, but we had a match to prepare for, and that was our priority.

“But I think we were all really enthusiastic about the new stadium, I think everyone can say that. Inter, for me, is that team we were talking about: a team that can play with their eyes closed, that rotates, like in the last match in midfield, and continues to express themselves in exactly the same way.

“Certain individual characteristics change, but they already know what to do on the pitch even without needing to practice too much. They have an extraordinary ability to read the moments of the game.

“You can clearly sense that, even if they find themselves behind late on, they have the maturity to understand that they can win any match: it’s an awareness you gain when you win so many matches and so many titles.

“They have a lot of talent in their squad, but we’re there to fight against that too and we’ll be ready for the match.”

Goncalo Ramos scored a brace against you in a derby between Benfica and Sporting CP with you on the bench. Could he also be the man for the Milan derby?

“I think it could be. I think all the problems and difficulties Goncalo Ramos is experiencing are primarily a team issue. I think we need to push forward… We control games well, but we play too far from the opponent’s goal.

“We need to raise our centre of gravity and the team on the pitch, spending more time in that area of ​​the pitch to allow Ramos to play his game. He’s playing far from the goal because the team can’t push the opponent in the final thirty metres. I think we need time to correct this aspect as well.

“We want to do better and we will improve in this area. But in any match, a player like Goncalo Ramos, who has already shown he can break the deadlock at any moment and score in any situation, can be the man of the match in the next one.”

Why did you reduce the squad so much at the start of the season? Do you regret it?

“When it happens, you think about it, but these are things you can’t control. There are factors that are beyond your control. Think about Saelemaekers, who had that physical problem practically at the end of a training match during the international break.

“Then Chukwueze comes along with another problem, and as a result Moreira ends up being overworked because he’s forced to play more minutes since Chukwueze and Saelemaekers aren’t there. Imagine having three players for a single position and all three get injured: at that point you overload that department.

“And then you take that player and make your rotations, and you find yourself fielding Tomori… well, I’m not saying as a winger, but adapted to emergency situations, maybe having him do an extra 400-meter sprint.

“Then obviously I take the risk because I want to win against Bologna, I know perfectly well that we can’t afford to lose other players and that certain characteristics were needed for that specific match. So I pushed for Tomori and we found ourselves with this problem.

“I think that sometimes Some things simply can’t be controlled; you have to imagine them. In my head, at the beginning, I had three options for that role, and all three had physical problems: when that happens, you can’t manage the impossible.

“Unless you have a squad of forty players, but then you have to deal with financial management, with each player’s playing time, or you have to accept taking some risks, taking a gamble. Today, if I could go back, maybe I’d want a few more players.

“But if we look at the situation rationally – and we have to be rational – the numbers at the start of the week told us we were fine with the rotations; but then in the last week, with three games in a few days, we found ourselves with six or seven starters or key players out of action.

“It’s a situation you can’t control. So, to answer the question: yes, maybe we’re short on resources right now, but there’s always a rational logic behind every decision made at the start of the season.”

Ramos gets fouled a lot. Should he become a bit more aggressive too?

“I like the way we’re going here in Italy, we’re on the right path. More speed, fewer fouls: I think it’s an evolution that’s improving the quality of the game. Sometimes you might think that maybe that could be a foul, but I like it that way.

“And then, I’m not going to talk about the referees: just take the images of the Udinese match and compare them with those of other games. I won’t say a single word more and you’ll understand exactly what I mean. But I won’t comment on the referees, I want to be crystal clear.

“I like this kind of approach, I like that in Serie A we see results like 5-1, 4-4, 3-3: I think it’s really a great advertisement for our country and for our movement. However, if you look at what happened with Udinese and compare it to other matches, well…

“Maybe it’s becoming difficult for Ramos to have more touches of the ball, maybe it’s difficult for Ramos to move freely inside the penalty area. Take the images, do the comparison, and then make your own evaluations and decisions.”

A bit of defensive fragility has also been evident in recent matches…

“In Bournemouth, we conceded two goals from penalties and one from a free kick, having been down a man for the entire match.

“Against Bologna, however, we conceded the fourth goal in seven minutes: we were completely out of position, and instead we had to maintain our identity until the last second, because we were buying time to reopen and turn the game around.

“Conceding a 3-2 is not the same as conceding a 4-2, and we still had plenty of time to recover. My feeling is that after the 3-2, we became anxious, starting to lose our composure and overturn our positions on the pitch.

“The central defenders going up with the ball, Pavlovic running forward with the ball, all these little flaws are details that we absolutely must correct in training, talking about them openly.

“It takes that collective maturity to understand that yes, the momentum of the game has changed, but we had 40 minutes left to fix it because we would have created chances anyway. Different situations, different dynamics. on which we must inevitably grow as a team: this is a clear fact.”

“Injuries and muscle problems have nothing to do with the medical staff, the gym staff, or Milan Lab. The responsibility lies with me, the coach, and the way he trains the team.

“What I can say is that there are several situations to consider: overloading certain areas forces us to take risks, and then we need to thoroughly analyse the medical history of individual players.

“Take, for example, those who say that a player like Cisse doesn’t play, scores a goal, and then misses the next match: we need to look at his history, the pubalgia problems, the serious injuries he’s suffered in the last year, and it’s my duty to manage him accordingly.

“We need to consider how many consecutive matches these players have played in the past, how many meters of sprint they complete, whether it’s the same type of effort or whether the game has changed.

“It’s the combination of all these factors that causes injuries. And then there’s bad luck: when you suffer a foot problem, it’s pure and simple bad luck. I’ll tell you: the episode that happened to Saelemaekers was just bad luck.

“When you find yourself With one less option at a certain position, you can’t rotate the players as you’d like, and then things happen. But I want to say this very clearly: the medical staff is extraordinary, they’re doing an exceptional job and they work hard every single day.

“Workload management is my job, it’s my responsibility. I know the medical history of every player on the roster, I know the daily workload, and I try to manage it as best I can. Sometimes, however, I’m forced to take risks, or there are guys who aren’t used to playing so many games in a row.

“Take a player like Jashari: he’s played three games, two of them 90 minutes, without any problems. Others, however, play a half and a half and are already feeling the fatigue.

“We try to monitor and manage all of this with the utmost attention, but I repeat: I’m very happy with our medical staff and they’re doing an incredible job.”

Why these ups and downs in performance and results?

“It’s a combination of factors that combine. Of course, we need to develop the maturity needed to control matches and manage the various moments of a match, and we’ll get there with time.

“Then there’s the busy schedule and the simultaneous injury crisis: a situation that doesn’t make our game any easier, because to perform at our best, we need certain technical and physical characteristics. I think it’s truly a combination of all of these.

“We need to pay attention to every single detail; we need to train more, spend more time talking and working on these aspects. But right now, we don’t even have time to fully recover, let alone do targeted training sessions.

“That’s why we’re having so many difficulties in some matches: to find that consistency of performance, we need to address and correct all these issues during the week, but we don’t have the time. Despite everything, I assure you that we will become a great team.”

Will the substitutions be one of the keys to the match? How is the team’s spirit?

“Regarding the second question, I sensed the right mentality in the players. Yesterday we were bitter, we were angry: more than bitter, we were truly furious. I myself was very angry yesterday, and it’s difficult to start over the next day.

“Today, however, I saw them completely focused on the match against Inter, concentrating on technical and tactical training, because that’s all that matters now. They were extremely attentive and have a clear understanding of the game plan and what needs to be done.

“In terms of attitude and mentality, this team is on the right path. If we analyze our performances, various types of difficulties emerge. There are games where we start terribly and finish on a high, like against Lazio, and others where we play excellent 66 minutes, like against Atalanta, only to then drop in intensity.

“Sometimes it’s more a question of psychological momentum than chronological playing time. The key is to find consistency throughout the entire 90 minutes. We don’t yet have the same experience and maturity as Inter: it’s It’s an obvious fact, and we must acknowledge it pragmatically.

“When Inter find themselves in trouble towards the end, they tend to fill the penalty area, pushing many players forward and using crosses to overload the opposition’s defenses. Our playing style is different; we’re not that type of team.

“So both tactical and technical aspects come into play. We simply need to focus on being consistent throughout the match, because so far we’ve shown different sides depending on the game: sometimes we start strong and then fade, other times we start poorly like against Lazio and improve in the second half.

“We need to become a better team, more mature and capable of reading and interpreting the various moments of the game.”

#2013. Sunday's Serie A predictions including Juventus vs. Napoli, Lazio vs. Cagliari

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 00:30

Today's Serie A predictions include Luciano Spalletti and Max Allegri taking on their former clubs, with Juventus facing Napoli in the standout match, as well as title-contending Lazio welcoming Cagliari to the capital.

Arriving at Stadio Sinigaglia in starkly contrasting form, high-flying Como and rock-bottom Venezia will meet for Serie A's Sunday lunchtime kickoff.

While the hosts won again in midweek, and stayed in touch with Italy's top three, their Venetian visitors lost for the eighth time this term.

While Venezia have generally offered some resistance at Stadio Penzo, they are yet to pick up a point on the road - and that drought will go on.

Como may be feeling the strain of a packed fixture list - and several fringe players are injured - but their sheer weight of individual skill usually shines through.

After racking up 13 goals in three games, free-scoring Frosinone will aim to extend their strong start in Serie A when they welcome Torino to Stadio Stirpe on Sunday.   Sitting four points above their visitors, the newly promoted side are surpassing all expectations, but Toro's own winning run was abruptly halted in midweek.

Generally tipped for relegation in August, Frosinone have quickly become a team to fear, smashing goals past several opponents.

Yet, after a grim 2025-26 campaign, Torino are showing signs of improvement under new boss Abate - and they have had two extra days to recover.

Lazio will look to prolong an incredible start to the Serie A season on Sunday, when they welcome Cagliari to Stadio Olimpico.

For the first time since they last lifted the Scudetto, the Biancocelesti are unbeaten through their first nine league games; meanwhile, the visitors remain in Rome after suffering another defeat in midweek.

While Lazio cannot stop scoring, Cagliari have begun to leak goals at an alarming rate, and that is not a good combination for the Sardinian side.

So, the hosts' success streak will go on, while the visitors are set for their second loss in Rome within the space of five days.

Fresh from securing consecutive Serie A victories for the first time this season, Genoa travel to Lecce on Sunday aiming to claim a third straight league win on matchday 10.

Daniele De Rossi's men will certainly be in higher spirits than the Salentini, who have suffered back-to-back defeats after falling 5-1 to early-season high-flyers Frosinone on Thursday.

Thursday's heavy defeat was alarming, but Lecce have repeatedly demonstrated an ability to recover from successive setbacks and should produce a more disciplined home performance.

Genoa's six-match winless away run and five blanks during that sequence suggest that their recent revival may stall at Stadio Via del Mare.

Headlining Serie A's ninth round, Italian giants Juventus and Napoli will convene in Turin for a heavyweight contest on Sunday.

Both coaches have a glorious past with the other club, but that must be forgotten when three points are at stake - particularly with the pair trailing Italy's top six.

Traditionally, the home side prevails when this pair clash, but Juventus are currently low in confidence and could be facing another defeat.

Napoli have unlocked more firepower since returning from the last international break, and that should help them outscore their ailing hosts.

#2012. Scott Bain on Scotland No.1 hopes, beating Celtic and his love for Falkirk

Falkirk's stunning 2-0 win over Celtic was built on discipline, resilience and a goalkeeping performance that Scott Bain admits ranks among the very best of his career.

The former Celtic keeper was in inspired form against his old club, producing a string of saves as John McGlynn's side claimed a famous victory over the Premiership champions. The result stretched Falkirk's winning run to four games and delivered a third consecutive clean sheet, with Bain at the heart of it all.

Having spent seven years at Celtic, where he was often a spectator for long spells, the 34-year-old relished being called into action and believed the display showcased the best of his shot-stopping ability.

"It was a busy day. It was an amazing result, four wins in a row and three clean sheets in a row. Amazing for the team, amazing for the club and the manager and, for myself, just delighted with the performance.

"We can take so much belief from that game. I really enjoyed the game. I had an early save and then one just before half-time from Duran. When we came out in the second half I thought it was going to be backs against the wall.

"I thought we defended excellently. We put our bodies in front of things, we cleared things and I just felt it was one of those games where they weren't going to score. Thankfully they never.

"When it got to about the 77th minute I thought we were going to be fine. They put us under a lot of pressure and put balls in the box, but I thought our togetherness, our team spirit and also our quality when we won the ball back at times was excellent.

"We outfought them at times and we also outplayed them at times. It was really good."

When asked if it was the finest display of his career, Bain admitted Sunday's performance was certainly in the conversation.

"It was probably the most saves I've made in a game. I had one against Dundee United that was similar this season where we never really managed to hold on.

"But I thought there we looked really comfortable in the end, although I'm having to make these saves.

"When it got down to the nitty-gritty of the last five minutes I thought we looked quite comfortable."

Bain's form has not gone unnoticed. Falkirk supporters repeatedly sang his name during the victory and even hailed him as Scotland's No.1, although the goalkeeper is not interested in making grand claims about displacing those ahead of him in the international pecking order.

The keeper, who has four Scotland caps, hopes his performances can earn him another call-up from Sebastien Pocognoli and admits he thoroughly enjoys being involved with the national squad.

"The fans have been brilliant with me," he said. "When I came here it probably took me a couple of games to get going and they stood by me. I feel really comfortable going into games and I feel like I'm performing really well, so it's nice that they sing that.

"I hope that I'm in the next squad. I really enjoyed working with the manager and seeing his ideas and how he works.

"As long as I go away and put my best foot forward, I'm happy to give my best account of myself out there."

Bain is widely regarded as one of the best ball-playing goalkeepers in Scotland, but against Celtic it was the more traditional side of his game that took centre stage.

"We didn't really play out from the back as much as we normally would, but I think it's a given that people know it's one of my strongest attributes.

"I've got most of the clubs in the bag, but sometimes I slice it off the tee.

"We never really did that. It was more about the nitty-gritty and I managed to make a lot of saves, so it was a good showcase in terms of saves. I'm really enjoying my time here and I feel really comfortable in the goals at the minute."

For now, Bain knows any Scotland ambitions depend on maintaining the level he has reached in recent weeks for a Falkirk side enjoying a strong spell of form.

"It's difficult because with international football you can only do what you can do for your club and hopefully the manager sees that and makes a decision.

"I don't ever go there expecting to play. I go there to represent myself the best I can and I play these games for Falkirk to represent myself the best I can.

"Whether that turns out with the manager giving me some game time when we're away then I'll do my best if I get the opportunity. But mostly, international football for me is about what I do here. Can I put in good performances to be in the conversation? That's really what it's about."

#2011. Alvaro Arbeloa makes bold "we can beat anyone" claim after Fulham end Villa Park losing run

By Ben Sully | 01 Nov 2026 00:39, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 02:17

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has expressed his belief that his team "can beat anyone" after they held Aston Villa to a 1-1 draw on Saturday.

The Cottagers were fortunate not to fall behind in the early stages at Villa Park as John McGinn crashed his 16th-minute penalty against the frame of the goal.

Villa eventually opened the scoring through Nicolas Jackson in the closing stages of the first period, before Fulham responded with a lengthy spell of consistent pressure after the restart.

The Cottagers deservedly levelled the scoreline just after the hour mark, although the goal arrived in fortuitous circumstances as Zion Suzuki dropped the ball over the line as he attempted to gather from a corner.

While they were unable to find a winner, the draw ended Fulham's seven-game losing run at Villa Park since they last won at the ground in 2014.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! ? https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Fulham finished the game with 55% possession, five shots on target to Villa's three and an xG of 2.21 compared to the opposition's 1.71.

The encouraging performance represented another building block in Alvaro Arbeloa's tenure as his side made it three consecutive Premier League games without a win.

Speaking after the game, the Fulham boss declared that his players have proven they are capable of competing with any team put in front of them.

"I am so happy with our performance in the second half," Arbeloa said. "This is what I want to see from my team, that character, that ambition.

"We needed to be aggressive against a team like Villa. It was a Champions League team in front of us.

"Technically, I thought we were very good but this is the Premier League, and you have to be aggressive, and physically, you have to be at your best level.

"I think maybe we deserved a little bit more, but the performance was really great. I think we are a very difficult team to beat, and I think we can beat anyone."

Having picked up seven points from their last three games, Fulham sit outside the Premier League drop zone in 15th, but they cannot rest on their laurels, with only two points separating them from the bottom three.

Arbeloa's charge will turn their focus to a home clash against Newcastle United on Saturday, November 7.

That will be their final outing before the international window, and it will be key to pick up a positive result before they return to action with a tricky run of fixtures after the two-week break.

Fulham take on Manchester City on November 21, before going up against two teams currently in form in the shape of Bournemouth and Tottenham Hotspur.
