#2010. Cardinale explains what he has learned as AC Milan owner and what he still wants to achieve

Gerry Cardinale has shed some light on the ‘learning curve’ of being AC Milan’s owner, as well as some of the plans he has for the future.

It has been a bit of a different past few months for Cardinale compared to his first few years with Milan. The owner has chosen to become more hands-on in his involvement, overseeing decisions such as the managerial clear-out at the end of last season and the hiring of Ruben Amorim.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For the American, the vision remains to get Milan back to the top of Italian football. This morning he stressed in another interview that Amorim will be given time and will be backed with more signings, such is his belief that the Portuguese is the right man for the new era.

Cardinale was interviewed by ClassCNBC, a channel that broadcasts financial and economic news from around the world 24 hours a day. He spoke about various topics connected to Milan, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

What does the new stadium represent for you and the project?

“It’s a long journey: we’ve owned the club for four years and have been implementing this plan since day one, aware that to bring Milan back to where it deserves to be – at the top of Serie A and among Europe’s elite – every single aspect must be transformed: the live event, the fan experience, the infrastructure for the players.

“It’s an entire ecosystem that must be renewed and modernized to keep pace with the times. We have enormous respect for the history and culture that San Siro embodies, but our goal is to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“If we want the stadium to be a tribute to the tradition and legacy of one of the most important brands in world sport, the infrastructure and the new facility must evolve in tandem: this has been the heart of the project from day one.”

How do you protect the assets of a club like AC Milan while also projecting them into the future?

“That’s a great question; we think about it all the time. Ultimately, there’s the infrastructure, and then there’s how you bring it to life: the hardware and the software. The answer lies entirely in the software. And the software is the people, the fans, that unique energy.

“An energy that, even for an American like me, accustomed to top-level US sports, when you experience it at San Siro with the people, is unparalleled in the world. I think any American would agree.

“We can bring our strategic model, but it only works if we have a profound respect for this heritage. We engage with the community to understand what’s truly fundamental: there’s a legendary history here, and we’ll do everything we can to live up to an iconic name like San Siro.”

You talk about a ‘sports and entertainment’ platform. Where do you draw the line between the worlds of sports and entertainment?

“Sports and entertainment are increasingly intertwined. The reason? The cost of TV rights and club valuations have risen to the point that entertainment is becoming indispensable to supporting the sporting side of things.

“But the real reason we’re doing all this is to bridge the economic gap with the Premier League. The secret of European football is that the Premier League has gained a lead over the rest of the continent, and we in Europe are all in the same boat.

“It’s a general problem in sports, also present in the United States: the gap between large and small markets, between rich and less wealthy clubs, continues to widen due to media rights.

“Entertainment, if managed properly and without ever losing sight of the centrality of the pitch, is the fundamental lever for generating the resources needed to finance a competitive team.”

Will modern infrastructure be enough to bridge the gap with the Premier League, or is it primarily a cultural issue?

“It’s the sum of all things. We start from a very simple premise: Italian football absolutely needs to change, and this change must act as a driving force for the entire ecosystem.

“There’s a huge amount of work to do, and as AC Milan we have the responsibility to be the pace car, the point of reference for change and innovation. Terms that often scare many people, but which, if channeled and managed well, represent a huge benefit.

“It’s the same concept as what we’re doing in Hollywood right now: often those in power consolidate the status quo and don’t want change or innovation; they don’t wake up in the morning with a sense of urgency.

“But if you don’t do that, Netflix overwhelms Hollywood, and the Premier League takes over the continental leagues. Our work and our investment approach consist precisely in entering these ecosystems to innovate them.

“Doing so with a club like AC Milan is a great privilege and an extraordinary opportunity, because we have a profound respect for what has been, with the aim of bring it back to its past levels.”

What is the club’s financial health, considering the €50 million equity injection? Will further capital injections be needed in the future?

“What I can say is that we remain in control of our financial health. The decision to close in the red this summer was my own, made the day after we were eliminated from the Champions League, when I took direct operational control of the club.

“Looking at how things had been going over the last four years, I realied that the time had come for real change. And I wasn’t willing to implement structural changes in a matter of weeks, between the end of the season and the transfer window, as almost all clubs do.

“I didn’t want to delegate such a revolution to an external structure in such a short timeframe: these are too important organisational decisions, so I decided to intervene personally. At the same time, I chose to restructure and re-establish the sporting area.

“We have retained and developed several key players, brought in new ones, and lowered the average age of the squad. The reality is that, just as with TV rights, there has been a strong inflation in player salaries: it’s up to us to decide whether we want to compete to win, and we must accept these dynamics.

“For this year, we chose to go into the red, but we will return to the red very quickly once we have consolidated the organizational structure, managing incoming and outgoing transfer operations as best as possible, and maintaining commercial momentum.

“Recently, I have focused heavily on the sporting and football aspects, but we also bring a wealth of expertise to the business side. When we acquired the club in 2022, revenue was around €280m; we’ve increased it to over €400m, and we can still do a lot more, not least because the new stadium will provide a further, crucial boost in this direction.”

“They keep asking me questions like, ‘Are you having fun? Are you happy?’ My answer is a mixed one: I’m happy when we win, I enjoy it when we win, and right now we’re not winning enough.

“That said, this has been by far the most difficult challenge I’ve ever faced in my life, and I love challenges of this magnitude. The implications of a success here are monumental, and the ripple effect it would have for the local community, the country, the league, and the entire football landscape would be truly profound.

“The stadium, to give a concrete example, sends a message to the world and to international football of primary importance, particularly for Serie A and for Italy, precisely at a time when the movement isn’t performing up to its glorious tradition.

“For us, being able to position ourselves as a global leader with an infrastructure of this kind and with what it represents for the future is a fundamental objective.”

Do you intend to move forward by personally managing every aspect of the club, or do you think the club and the sports structure need a strong management figure, a technical director?

“That’s a great question. I wanted to clarify two key points. First, I will never hand over the keys to anyone again. From now on, I will always be operational and present in person. This is too important, and I can make too great a contribution, for that not to be the case.

“Second, however, is that I intend to do what I do best: one of my main tasks is organizational design, and our goal is to build a world-class football organization.

“Given what we represent and AC Milan’s history, we must be able to attract the best professionals on the market, and that’s exactly what we will do. So, we will continue to do both.”

Do you already have a specific name or profile in mind?

“It’s a question I get asked all the time. But it’s not just about naming names, and it’s curious how in football discussions, people always look for scoops on individual figures. I say that what really matters is the planning, the organizational architecture, what we’re building.

“As for names, I can only say that yes, I have some profiles in mind, but they will only become operational within and in accordance with the corporate model we’re designing, and that’s what I’m totally focused on.”

Do you also have player names in mind? Is he becoming increasingly expert in the art of selecting and acquiring players?

“Well, yes. If you’d told me a year ago that I’d be spending my time watching videos, interacting with scouts and our technical staff, I’d have been quite surprised, but it’s something that’s gotten under my skin now.

“The learning curve has been incredibly steep, but then again, if you look at what I’ve done with RedBird and throughout my career, it’s always been about building organizations made up of top-notch people.

“It means knowing how to negotiate, knowing how to manage financial considerations, making sure people are all pulling in the same direction to achieve the set goal. That’s exactly what football thrives on, and that’s what determines its success.

“It’s no different from what we do in the corporate world. It’s about doing things the right way, building a solid organization: and it’s not enough to win, it’s not enough to have a big name at the moment, you have to do it consistently.

“It means creating a structure that can constantly evolve, because the world doesn’t just sit back and wait for you. The Premier League will continue to grow stronger, and our job is to is keeping up.”

Looking back, how do you evaluate these four years at Milan? What were the things you did well, and what were the mistakes you wouldn’t repeat?

“Hindsight is wonderful, as we all know. If I could start over again, I’d like to have the same awareness I’ve gained over the past four years. When we bought the club four years ago, it had just won the Scudetto, and I thought the sporting and footballing aspects were already in place and working perfectly; so I focused on other priorities, like the new stadium and commercial development.

“The reality is that you have to take care of both things simultaneously, and you can’t take it for granted that the pitch is in order. So, if I could go back, as steep as the learning curve was, I would have dedicated the same amount of time to the sporting aspect from day one as I am now.

“But the advantage of having taken this path is that today I perfectly understand what needs to be done. The time I spent this summer personally managing the club gave me the opportunity to understand exactly which roles to include in the new technical area structure.

“I would take care of the commercial side with my eyes closed; the world of football, however, has its own art and science component, and now I’ve finally climbed that ladder. learning curve. Putting these two elements together, the sum of the parts will be significantly greater than the whole.”

Arsenal travel to Anfield to face Liverpool in a crucial Premier League showdown on Sunday afternoon.

Mikel Arteta's side are desperate to bounce back after suffering a historic penalty shootout defeat to fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday.

The North London club are dealing with several major fitness concerns ahead of the trip following Bukayo Saka's worrying quad issue against Bayern Munich.

However, the reigning Premier League champions have received a timely domestic boost with three doubtful first-team stars joining the travelling party.

Meanwhile, the club hierarchy have also been dealt a frustrating blow in the transfer market regarding a highly rated teenage prospect.

According to HandofArsenal on X, the Gunners have been actively tracking Paris Saint-Germain defensive sensation David Boly.

The 17-year-old right-back has emerged as one of the brightest prospects in the Parisian academy and recently broke into the senior setup.

Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta was reportedly monitoring his situation with a view to bringing the French talent to the English capital.

However, the report claims that Boly now looks to be signing a new long-term contract at the Parc des Princes as things stand.

This development will force the Premier League heavyweights to look elsewhere in their ongoing search for youthful defensive reinforcements.

While their pursuit of Boly appears to have stalled, Arteta will be encouraged by the sight of Noni Madueke, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis travelling to Merseyside.

#2008. Official: Christian Pulisic signs contract renewal with AC Milan until 2031

AC Milan have announced the contract renewal of Christian Pulisic, tying the American star to the club until 2031.

On Tuesday this week, the news broke that Pulisic’s contract renewal was imminent after ‘an agreement in principle’ had been reached between the parties. Sure enough, the No.11 arrived at Casa Milan yesterday to sign his new deal with the club.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As we highlighted in our latest newsletter, as Pulisic still benefits from the Growth Decree, the reported pay rise from €4m to €5m will not cost them a fortune. As opposed to €9.25m gross without the Decree, they will pay €6.55m.

On their website this afternoon, Milan announced the long-awaited news and confirmed that the new contract will run until 2031.

“AC Milan is pleased to announce that Christian Pulisic has extended his contract with the Club through June 30th, 2031.

“Since joining the Rossoneri in July 2023, Christian has established himself as a key member of the team, standing out for his technical ability, character, consistency and unwavering work ethic. His 44 goals in 141 appearances for the Rossoneri highlight both his importance to the team and his role in the Club’s future plans.

“Pulisic’s contract extension reflects a shared commitment to building on the progress made together in recent years, with the ambition to keep improving, achieve new milestones and write more memorable chapters in the Club’s history,” the statement reads.

With 44 goals and 28 assists in 144 games to his name, the 28-year-old has been a key player in the last few seasons and Milan believe that he’s about to enter his prime years. Securing the renewal was thus an important step forward for the club’s entire project.

#2007. Michael Carrick’s Man Utd misery compounded as continental rivals 'hijack' Old Trafford's succession masterplan

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 05:06

Manchester United could reportedly miss out on top managerial target Julian Nagelsmann following emerging interest from Italian giants Juventus.

The Red Devils extended their miserable winless streak across all competitions after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Xabi Alonso's side early in the second half before Cole Palmer doubled the advantage from the penalty spot.

A frustrating afternoon in West London was compounded when Lisandro Martinez received a red card for raising his forearm towards Wesley Fofana to concede the decisive spot kick.

Despite losing four of their last five matches, Michael Carrick has seemingly retained the backing of the Old Trafford board for the time being.

According to Italian journalist Rudy Galetti via Manchester Evening News, Juventus have officially registered their interest in Nagelsmann as they prepare for a potential change in the dugout.

Juventus are reportedly weighing up the prospect of dismissing head coach Luciano Spalletti, following a run of just two wins in their past seven matches.

The report names the former Bayern Munich and Germany manager as the club’s leading choice to oversee a much-needed revival in Turin.

Spalletti faces a pivotal Serie A meeting with Napoli on Sunday evening, with defeat at home potentially bringing his tenure to an end.

Juventus are also said to be keeping tabs on Didier Deschamps, Stefano Pioli, Sergio Conceicao and former boss Antonio Conte as possible alternatives.

Juventus’ unexpected move poses a major headache for United’s hierarchy as they cautiously consider their options for life after Carrick.

Nagelsmann had already emerged as one of the leading contenders for the Old Trafford vacancy, alongside Eddie Howe and Unai Emery.

Should the German coach accept a lucrative offer from the Serie A side, the Premier League strugglers would have to rethink their managerial shortlist considerably.

For now, Carrick is expected to take charge of a daunting Champions League tie against Roma on Tuesday evening.

The under-pressure Englishman thanked the travelling supporters for their full-time ovation at Stamford Bridge and said his side needed to take encouragement from the performance.

#2006. Steve Herbert: Let's hope this sorry season is about to come good

It’s taken two months but Crawley Town have finally felt that winning feeling again in the league.

A huge three points were earned at Boundary Park last weekend when a Danilo Orsi goal in the fifty second minute sent the three points back to West Sussex. It was a hard earned victory, and a tough watch, but the boys got the job done. Helped by the fact the Latics were reduced to nine men by halftime after two of their players had received marching orders. A lot of fans then presumed the Reds would go on and win quite comfortably, but that’s not how football works.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Think back to the beginning of August and our home game with Crewe, when we ourselves were reduced to nine men after Gordon and Ebiowei were sent off. It took the opposition a while to break us down, and when they did the goal was a huge slice of luck.

It was a similar story at Oldham but this time it was on the opposite foot. What was impressive was the managerial decision by interim boss Kevin Blackwell to substitute Kai Jennings in the first half after he’d picked up a yellow card. The referee was probably desperate to reduce the arrears. So by taking the player off it stopped the referee from making that happen and with it we kept eleven versus nine and the win was sealed. Clearly the locals weren’t happy and at full time an Oldham fan launched a crutch at the referee! Yes you have read that right, how the supporter made it home is anyone’s guess.

The success puts us to within three points of safety with a huge six pointer coming up at Rotherham on Saturday week. But prior to that our attention turns to the FA Cup and a trip to Dorset to face non league opponents in Wimborne Town. The tie has been moved to a Sunday and live tv, obviously because it reads FA Cup shock all over it. Wimborne Town FC have even built a new terrace on one side of the ground ahead of the game. After trips to Maidenhead United and Borehamwood in recent seasons, this is yet another cracking game to look forward to, and in all honesty we should be doing everything we can to make sure we make it to the second round. That’s where we can all start dreaming of progressing to face the big boys of the Premier League in round three.

What it also gives everyone is a nice distraction from a disastrous start to our League Two campaign.

Although after the win at Oldham let’s hope this sorry season is about to come good. See you all in Dorset on Sunday Reds fans.

Now, what happened Saturday? We picked up our second win of the season away to Oldham Athletic, albeit against ten men for seventy-six minutes and nine for an hour, with Danilo Orsi answering his critics in the best way possible by being in the right place to score after Charlie Barker had hit the woodwork with a thunderous drive from the edge of the box. For once it may have seemed that we got the rub of the green, and all I can say about that is, “about time”.

There was a lot of noise in my flat on Saturday afternoon and to the other residents I can only apologise and assure them that next Sunday it should be quiet as I will be in Wimborne, hopefully watching the Red Devils go three games unbeaten and progress to the 2nd round of the FA Cup.

A long way to go yet as we try and rescue our season, but with the return of Josh Flint and now being 17th in the form table, I really think we won’t have long to wait until we are out of the drop zone. Remember, "it ain't over till the overweight lady sings, so if you see her approaching, please point her in another direction"

#2003. Liverpool handed major boost as Crystal Palace face three-match ban nightmare over reckless tackle

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 01:20

Crystal Palace will be without influential striker Jean-Philippe Mateta for their forthcoming Premier League meeting with Liverpool.

The Frenchman is due to serve a three-match domestic ban after being sent off during Saturday's 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur.

Mateta was dismissed after only 13 minutes in North London, following a late challenge on Spurs captain Micky van de Ven.

The Palace forward's absence is a significant setback for the Eagles ahead of the daunting visit from Andoni Iraola's title-chasing Reds on November 8.

The flashpoint came as Van de Ven reached a loose ball ahead of his opponent before a late tackle caught him and also brought down Spurs teammate Jan Paul van Hecke.

Referee Michael Oliver first showed a yellow card, but VAR intervened and recommended an on-field review.

After watching the footage, Oliver changed his decision to a straight red for serious foul play, leaving the visitors to play more than 75 minutes with ten men.

The dismissal came shortly after Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky had kept out Palace’s first genuine opportunity of the evening.

The timing is particularly unfortunate for Mateta, who had only recently returned from injury and was left out of the club's midweek cup tie to manage his workload.

Without a powerful focal point like Mateta, Palace lose a vital reference in an attacking system built around his presence.

The former Mainz loanee was the club’s leading league scorer last season and has scored 50 top-flight goals since joining in January 2021.

Although his start to the current campaign has been disrupted, Palace still have options capable of troubling the Merseyside side.

Eddie Nketiah is likely to lead the attack after recently scoring the winning goal in a cup tie without Mateta, while Ismaila Sarr is set to shoulder more of the attacking responsibility.

#2002. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#2000. Liverpool vs. Arsenal: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League clash

By Lewis Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 04:32

Liverpool could find themselves in a battle for the Premier League title if they beat Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday.

Mikel Arteta's side come into the clash in second place with 21 points, six more than their fifth-placed hosts, and they will feel invigorated following Manchester City's loss against Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday.

Andoni Iraola will want to continue his side's impressive start to 2026-27, and moving three points behind the Gunners would fuel hopes of a title charge.

Here, Sports Mole provides all the details about how to watch Liverpool's clash with Arsenal.

This match kicks off at 4:30pm UK time on Sunday, November 1.

The Gunners will travel to Anfield, a stadium with a maximum capacity of 61,276.

The game will be broadcast live on the Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League TV channels.

Alternatively, fans can stream the action live via the Sky Sports+ app or through NOW TV if they have purchased the Sky Sports package on the online platform.

Game-changing events will be posted to the SkySportsPL X (formerly Twitter) account before highlights are made available on the Sky Sports app after full time.

Highlights will also be uploaded to the Sky Sports Premier League YouTube channel later in the day.

The title will not be won by either team after nine matchweeks, but both must seize on the opportunity that has presented itself.

Manchester City look far from their best, and they also appear likely to be sanctioned following news they were found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules on an industrial scale.

Arsenal will be seen as clear favourites for first if they claim a win on Sunday, but Liverpool have not lost against the visitors in the Premier League at Anfield since 2012.

Though Iraola's side have not been perfect this season, belief has been growing in the squad and fanbase that the team can achieve success, and perhaps success could be the Premier League title.

#1999. 'They'll be back': Scott Bain issues honest Celtic verdict after Falkirk heroics

Scott Bain knows a thing or two about Celtic crises. The goalkeeper spent almost a decade at Parkhead, with the infamous 2020/21 campaign a rare blemish on an otherwise admirable CV.

Bain won seven league titles, five Scottish Cups, and four League Cups with Celtic. He predominantly served as a back-up stopper throughout his spell at the club, registering 78 appearances in seven-and-a-half years.

He came back to haunt his ex-employers on Sunday, making nine saves as Falkirk recorded their first win over Celtic since 2007.

Martin O'Neill's side have now suffered six defeats in their last 10 matches, looking anything but a structured, effective unit.

Bain, though, insists he's seen Celtic in worse states, and that it won't 'take much' for them to once more become the 'unbeatable' team he played in.

"I feel sorry for boys in terms of it's a difficult place to be when it's not going well. But I've seen them worse," Bain said. "They've been worse and I was there when they were worse.

"So I think there's obviously overreaction at times with fans and things like that because it's a very emotional club and it's a club that's rooted deep in people's families and across generations. So they demand a lot of you.

"The only way to get through it is to stand up and puff your chest out and keep going, you can't buckle to the fans or the pressure or the results. They've been fine in the league.

"Obviously the last two results are a bit damning for them but in terms of the league I don't feel there's been any issues and I think maybe these little issues here have probably been brought on from outside noise and extra pressures on to the players.

"Obviously they've not performed as well in Europe as Celtic have recently, outwith your Champions League disasters, if I can say that."

Scott Bain greets Liam Scales after Falkirk's win over Celtic. (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock)

During what's now known as the Covid season, Bain played 23 times. It remains Celtic's only trophy-less campaign since 2009/10.

"I never felt the full brunt of it but the Covid season was really tough and that wasn't even fans in the stadium," Bain explained. "I think no fans made it even worse.

"But for the majority of my time there it's been sweet, the club was in a really good place and I think it'll maybe take a few signings here and there, a few ideas here and there and they'll be back there, I don't think it'll take much."

Bain left Celtic for Falkirk last summer. He's since become one of their most important players, earning a recall to the Scotland national team.

Inconsistency of minutes at Celtic, Bain says, made finding his peak form 'impossible'.

"When I played for Celtic we were really unbeatable when I played the majority of my games so I didn't really feel that until I came in with the signing of [Vasilis] Barkas and I played a game here and there, and I always found it difficult in general to play a game, come out of the team and play a game a few months later, play a couple of games here and come out.

"And then eventually I played a game once a year - what are you supposed to do with that? It's almost impossible."

"Could be, aye," was Bain's modest response when asked if Sunday was the best performance of his career.

Did any of his old Celtic chums, then, say anything post-match?

"They did, aye, a few expletives! No, they're obviously disappointed," Bain revealed. "It's a club that demands a lot of you.

"They created a lot of chances in the game and probably would win any sort of other game in that sense, it was just one of those days.

"But, look, I'm really tight with a lot of those boys and I've spent a lot of my life really with some of them. So they're disappointed but the boys that I know have congratulated me in terms of what a performance it was."

#1997. Pulisic insists he ‘always wanted to renew’ with Milan after confirmation: “Wanted to stay”

Christian Pulisic has finally signed a renewal to stay with AC Milan, and he spoke after it was confirmed this afternoon.

It’s a big day for Milan. After years of negotiations, Pulisic has put pen to paper on a new deal to signify his importance to the club. Indeed, the American has been in talks across three seasons over a new deal. Yet, nothing was ever officially done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Instead, talks broke down on two occasions and this felt like the final opportunity to agree on terms, even if a clause was available to extend his stay for another year past next summer.  Thankfully, that option was not needed, though, and the American has signed a new deal to keep him at San Siro until 2031.

Speaking to Sky Sport, via MilanNews, after the official confirmation of his renewal dropped, he admitted that he’d always hoped to renew his deal at San Siro, as well as looking ahead to the derby.

Your contract renewal until 2031 is now official. How happy are you?

“I’m very happy; renewing has always been my dream. I’ve always wanted to stay here, where I feel great confidence. I’m very happy here.”

Tomorrow is the derby, which is always a special match. What kind of match will it be?

“We know the derby is very intense; it’s a battle, and it will be the same tomorrow. I always want to score, not just in the derby. I want to help the team. We want to win.”

“We know that Inter have won a lot in recent years and that they play very well. Since I’ve been here, I’ve always seen them like this: a team that always plays well, always at the same level, and that deserves respect.

“But for us, the important thing is to focus on ourselves and put in a good performance tomorrow. If we do things right, we have a chance to win.”

What do you think of AC Milan and Amorim’s project?

“Yes, we always want to win: it can’t be any different with this jersey. It’s clear that it takes time, because there’s a new coach with new ideas, but we also want to win right away.

“We have a good relationship with the staff and the coach, we’re very happy and we’re learning something every day. Now we have to keep improving and win the championship.”

“A dream? Right now, it’s still the same dream, the same one as when I arrived.”

#1995. Sunday’s Bundesliga predictions including Eintracht Frankfurt vs. Hamburger SV, Union Berlin vs. FC Koln

By Lewis Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 04:46

Today's Bundesliga predictions will focus on the battle at the bottom, with Union Berlin set welcome FC Koln, before Eintracht Frankfurt host Hamburger SV.

Union Berlin vs. FC Koln (Sunday, 2:30pm)

Facing off for the second time this week, Union Berlin will welcome Bundesliga rivals FC Koln to Stadion An der Alten Forsterei on Sunday.

Die Eisernen are looking for a first win in four games, while the Billy Goats are hoping to build on their DFB-Pokal triumph over the hosts.

Union may have been hammered by Koln in midweek, but they have proven resilient in recent Bundesliga matches, and will be hoping to bounce back with a stronger showing in front of a home crowd.

Koln have struggled on the road this season, losing each of their three away league matches to date, and a draw would mark an improvement in that regard.

Eintracht Frankfurt boss Adi Hutter will be under immense pressure if his side lose against visitors Hamburger SV in the Bundesliga on Sunday at Deutsche Bank Park.

The hosts come into the clash in 14th place with just eight points, and while they are only one point from 11th-placed Hamburger, a defeat could leave them in the bottom three this weekend.

Frankfurt have been far from their consistent best this season, and their lack of firepower in recent weeks has been worrying.

Hamburger will be missing some of their best forwards on Sunday, and given they have rarely travelled well, perhaps the hosts will defeat the visitors once again.

#1994. How many games Michael Carrick has to save Man United job as 'private pledge' revealed

By Ben Knapton | 01 Nov 2026 07:04

Manchester United reportedly intend to give Michael Carrick at least two more games to save his job following Saturday's 2-0 Premier League loss to Chelsea.

The Red Devils hierarchy stuck by the popular Carrick after last weekend's harrowing 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, but their decision was not vindicated at Stamford Bridge.

Man Utd had the better of the first-half action against Xabi Alonso's side, but Morgan Rogers's opener, Lisandro Martinez's red card and Cole Palmer's penalty condemned the 20-time English champions to yet another defeat.

Only goal difference is keeping the Red Devils above the relegation zone in the Premier League table, where Carrick's men are languishing in 17th spot with just seven points from their opening nine games.

As well as losing three straight matches in all tournaments, Man United are winless in nine since thrashing Sabah 4-0 in the Champions League on September 10, and they have not won a single away contest in 2026-27.

However, having granted Carrick a stay of execution last month, The Athletic reports that the Man Utd hierarchy want to get to the November international break before making any major decisions on their next manager.

Carrick can therefore expect to take charge of Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma and next Sunday's Premier League showdown with Aston Villa, as the Red Devils board have 'privately pledged' to give the Englishman more time to turn the club's fortunes around.

Dissatisfactory results in one or both of those matches could trigger a change from the top, though, and club chiefs are actively considering alternative managers while Carrick struggles to get a tune out of his players.

The Englishman retains the backing of Man United fans, though, which is more than can be said for chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, both of whom were present at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Carrick was appointed permanent head coach on a two-year contract in the summer, having guided the Red Devils to a third-placed finish in the 2025-26 Premier League season with 11 wins from their final 16 games.

However, Man Utd have won just two of their 13 matches in all tournaments in 2026-27, while drawing four and losing seven, giving Carrick a measly return of 0.77 points per game.

Among the names the Red Devils are considering to succeed Carrick is Julian Nagelsmann, but Man Utd have suffered a blow in their pursuit of the ex-Germany manager, who has been contacted by Juventus.

Eddie Howe is also seen as a leading contender to take the reins at Man Utd, although Newcastle United would be due around £3m in compensation if the Red Devils hire the Englishman.

Ex-Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Antonio Conte has been strongly linked with the role too, but he recently released a statement denying he was in advanced talks with Man United.

#1993. I watched Celtic lose to Falkirk and noted telling Chris Sutton comments and a magic wand in decline

Celtic lost for the second time in the league this season as they were beaten 2-0 away to a Falkirk side who celebrated victory in this fixture for the first time since 2007.

The champions were unable to stretch their lead at the top of the Premiership, with nearest challengers Rangers on Premier Sports Cup duty.

Here are a few talking points from the match:

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sitting four points clear at the top just weeks after a 7-1 thrashing of a title rival wouldn’t usually be the sort of scenario worthy of cracked crests and furrowed brows. But there is something evidently deeply wrong with Celtic at this moment and it’s not entirely clear how to fix it.

Coming from behind to defeat Hibs and draw with Dundee United had helped to paper over the cracks but there would be no victory on this occasion to mask another under-par performance. Celtic gifted Falkirk an early goal and then were easily cut open for the second, while missing a raft of chances at the other end.

The statistics make for grim reading. They have now won just three of their last 10 games in all competitions, losing six of them. European football has become a burden rather than a pleasure, ever since the Champions League capitulation to LASK. The Europa League visit of Besiktas to Celtic Park on Thursday now becomes an occasion to be feared and not excitedly anticipated.

Martin O’Neill saved their bacon last season – twice – but seems to have lost his magic touch. Team selections alter every week, while half-time substitutions – often to fix tactical failings - are now commonplace. When even someone like Chris Sutton, so often an O’Neill ally, says on television that Celtic are “in regression” as a club then it just underlines the fact that all is not well.

A parting of the ways between manager and club now seems inevitable but it remains to be seen which party chooses to cut the cord first and when.

No team has scored more than Celtic’s 27 goals in the Premiership this season but that tally could and should be a lot higher. They were especially wasteful against Falkirk, offloading 24 shots, landing nine on target but failing to score with any of them.

Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain played the game of his life but, even still, there was a wastefulness about Celtic. Camilo Duran started through the middle but couldn’t finish any of the opportunities that came his way. Callum Osmand was removed at half-time after failing to make any significant contribution down the left, Haissem Hassan spent most of the game looking for fouls and throwing tantrums while Kasper Hogh made a negligible impact off the bench.

At 64, John McGlynn is just a year older than Jose Mourinho, recently appointed as Real Madrid manager, and Everton boss David Moyes. And yet there never seems to be much clamour around the Falkirk manager whenever vacancies crop up despite his incredible record in the last few years in steering the Bairns from League One to the giddy heights of fourth in the Premiership.

Appointing younger managers seems to be all the rage these days – Craig McLeish, Marink Reedijk and Alfred Johansson are all still in their 30s – but it feels like McGlynn deserves greater recognition of what he’s achieved, regardless of age.

Midhurst and Easebourne said in a statement on Saturday night: “Following the abandonment of our community team fixture this afternoon at the Rotherfield in the Malcolm Simmonds Memorial Cup, we can confirm that two Midhurst players were involved in a serious incident, with one requiring hospital treatment. “As a club we are deeply shocked that an incident of this nature has occurred during a game that should be enjoyed by everyone involved.

"We would like to extend our sincere thanks to South East Coast Ambulance Service and the club’s first aid-trained staff, who provided outstanding care and support to our player and his family during a very difficult situation.

"We are working closely with Sussex Police and the West Sussex Football Club as enquiries continue. Our priority remains the wellbeing and recovery of the player involved.

A further statement on Sunday afternoon revealed the extent of a player’s injuries.

The new Midhurst and Easebourne FC statement said: “Unfortunately two of our players were assaulted by yesterday’s opposition in a completely unprovoked attack. This led to one of our team members requiring urgent medical treatment after the serious injuries he received.

"We are now pleased to say he has been discharged from hospital after suffering severe damage to his internal mouth, a broken bone in his jaw, and a high chance of requiring surgery to fix the injury further.

"We would also like to thank again the South East Coast Ambulance Service for their swift response, and all of the medical team at the accident and emergency department.

"As a club we will continue to be working closely with Sussex Police and the West Sussex Football League to make sure the corrrect sanctions are carried out, and make sure we protect any further teams from having to put their players at such risk playing the game we enjoy.

That moment eventually arrived in the 83rd minute through Ryan Naderi and the man who provided the assist, James Penrice, believes such attributes are becoming increasingly evident within the squad and are helping to foster a winning mentality.

“When you're on the pitch and you play for Rangers, you should go until the end of the game,” he said. “You've seen that a couple of times. The resilience to keep going to the end, keep pushing. They made it very hard for us, but I think we got our reward. Ryan gets his strikers goal and it's a massive positive.”

Having already swept Celtic aside, Rangers knew the importance of backing up that emphatic 3-0 victory. Defeat in the semi-final against a struggling Dons side would have undermined much of the positivity generated by their quarter-final success, making the assignment another significant test of their character and credentials.

Penrice acknowledged that reaching Hampden was particularly important for those members of the squad experiencing such an occasion for the first time. He believes the occasion will provide added motivation ahead of their return to the national stadium in six weeks’ time, when they will be expected to justify their favourites' billing against Hibs.

“That was big. For a lot of the boys, it's their first time being at Hampden,” stated the 27-year-old. “It's massive that they experience that and it will help them want it more. It's special seeing boys that haven't seen those kind of scenes before, haven't seen Rangers at Hampden. It can only help us, and I think it will be ten times that if you were to come back here and win it. So that's the motivation for the boys is to relive that again.”

That appetite for success could prove a major factor in the weeks ahead. Rangers now have another outing at Hampden to anticipate in mid-December, but former Hearts man Penrice is under no illusion that reaching the final guarantees anyone a place in the starting XI. Quite the opposite, in fact.

With several players edging closer to a return from injury, competition for places is expected to intensify, ensuring nobody can afford to become complacent. It is a scenario Penrice welcomes.

“When you come back here in six weeks, everyone should be pushing. Pushing to try and get in the starting 11, pushing to get on the bench,” he explained. “You need two or three players in each position fighting for a jersey. And good enough to fight for a jersey. All wanting to win, all wanting to play and I think that's the main thing.”

Penrice has also shown a willingness to embrace a different challenge, having been deployed in midfield on a couple of occasions despite being more accustomed to operating in defence. His readiness to adapt to an unfamiliar role underlines his determination to contribute wherever required.

“It was obviously not what I've been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there's no question I'll play wherever,” he declared. “Whatever I can do to help the team is what I'll do. Obviously, it's not a position I've played in before in the past for Livingston and Partick. But if he asks me to play in there, I'm going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

That mentality will be essential. While being favourites to lift the trophy inevitably brings expectation, it also carries responsibility, and having negotiated the semi-final hurdle, they must now prove they can deliver when silverware is at stake.

Reaching a cup final so early in his Ibrox career offered Penrice further confirmation that his decision to move to Ibrox from AEK Athens in the summer was the right one.

“It was never in doubt. Never,” he exclaimed. “It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed hell of a lot. This is why I wanted to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

#1989. Burgess Hill 4s show grit and determination to defeat strong Hailsham 3s

Burgess Hill 4s produced a determined and disciplined team performance to secure a hard-earned 1-0 victory over a strong Hailsham 3s side in an entertaining and closely contested match.

The game was evenly balanced throughout much of the first half, with both teams creating attacking opportunities and moving the ball well. Burgess Hill looked dangerous going forward through the combination of Cath Donovan, Becs Marriner and Sabine Rowan, while Hailsham continually tested the home side with their pace and movement. As the game developed, Burgess Hill enjoyed several promising attacking spells of their own, forcing Hailsham onto the back foot and demonstrating plenty of attacking intent.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Behind them, the midfield unit of Gillian Branagan, Jo Richardson, Debs Scott and Toni Frier worked tirelessly to ensure Burgess Hill remained competitive in the middle of the pitch. Branagan had an outstanding game in the centre, repeatedly breaking up Hailsham attacks and distributing the ball intelligently into attacking areas. Scott worked relentlessly across the pitch, competing strongly for every loose ball and providing support in both attack and defence. Richardson provided calmness and composure whenever Burgess Hill were in possession, helping her side maintain shape and move the ball effectively, while Frier's energy and determination helped drive the team forward and disrupt Hailsham's rhythm.

At the other end of the pitch, Burgess Hill's defence produced an outstanding display. Sarah Bailey was tireless on the right-hand side, combining strong defensive work with energetic forward runs to support attacks before tracking back quickly to close down danger. On the left, Lucy Fox was rock solid throughout, producing a series of crucial clearances from inside the D and denying Hailsham attackers the opportunity to test the goalkeeper. Sweeping behind the defensive line, Wendy Caddye was calm and composed, reading the game superbly and consistently clearing danger before it developed into genuine opportunities. In the centre, Ali Gillham delivered an exceptional performance, producing a number of powerful and accurate clearances that bypassed the Hailsham midfield and found Burgess Hill's attackers, turning defence into attack with a single hit.

Also playing a vital role was goalkeeper Grace Mortimer, who communicated well with her defence throughout and showed great bravery coming off her line on several occasions to clear danger before Hailsham could capitalise.

The breakthrough came towards the end of the first half following an excellent team move. Branagan won possession in midfield and played a perfectly weighted pass to Marriner at the top of the D. Marriner showed great awareness to move the ball on to Donovan on the right side of the circle. Driving forward and facing the goalkeeper one-on-one, Donovan kept her composure before producing a perfectly timed slip pass across the face of goal. The move caught the goalkeeper off guard and found Rowan waiting unmarked at the left post, where she calmly guided the ball into the corner to give Burgess Hill a deserved 1-0 lead.

The second half proved even more challenging. Hailsham emerged determined to find an equaliser and increasingly applied pressure as the game wore on. Matters became even more difficult for Burgess Hill when Branagan was forced to leave the game midway through the half, leaving the side without a substitute. With Frier having sustained an earlier injury that limited her movement, the team had to dig deep physically and mentally to protect their advantage.

As Hailsham pushed forward, Burgess Hill showed tremendous resilience. Every player contributed, tracking back, making tackles and working for one another as Hailsham searched relentlessly for a way back into the contest.

The final stages of the game were particularly tense. Hailsham were awarded two consecutive short corners in the final two minutes, creating the best opportunities of the match to snatch a late equaliser. However, Burgess Hill defended superbly, with players charging out quickly, sticks down and bodies behind the ball to deny the initial strikes on goal.

The biggest moment of all came in the closing seconds. A lifted effort from Hailsham looked destined to find the net, but Mortimer reacted brilliantly, getting her pads to the ball and producing a vital save. Fox was quickest to react to the loose ball, clearing the danger and helping preserve Burgess Hill's slender lead.

After several nervous moments, the final whistle brought relief and celebration for the Burgess Hill side. Against a strong and determined Hailsham team, Burgess Hill had matched their opponents going forward, taken their chance when it came, and then shown outstanding character to defend their lead under immense late pressure.

While Rowan's goal ultimately secured the victory, this was very much a team performance. From the attacking pressure of Donovan, Marriner and Rowan, to the tireless efforts of the midfield and the heroic defensive display led by Bailey, Gilham, Fox, Caddye and Mortimer, every player played their part in a memorable and well-deserved 1-0 win.

Burgess Hill Team: Mortimer (GK), Marriner (C), Donovan, Branagan, Richardson, Frier, Caddye, Bailey, Gillham, Rowen, Scott, Fox. Player of the Match: Sarah Bailey
